Gomes scores for Aston Villa in defeat by Bayern Munich in Hong Kong

📅 07 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 16 min read (3281 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~16 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Aston Villa’s tour of the Far East ended in defeat as they lost 2-1 to German champions Bayern Munich in a pre-season friendly at the Kai Tak Sports Park in Hong Kong on Friday.
  • Bayern took the lead inside the final 10 minutes of the first half, with defender Kim Min-jae heading in from Tom Bischof’s sublime free-kick.
  • In a recent development, just as the game appeared to be out of reach for Aston Villa, who had struggled to create much going forward for most of the game, Unai Emery’s side demonstrated some life late on.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Aston Villa’s tour of the Far East ended in defeat as they lost 2-1 to German champions Bayern Munich in a pre-season friendly at the Kai Tak Sports Park in Hong Kong on Friday.

Bayern took the lead inside the final 10 minutes of the first half, with defender Kim Min-jae heading in from Tom Bischof’s sublime free-kick. Villa goalkeeper Marco Bizot made a string of saves in the second half to keep Bayern’s lead at one goal until former Liverpool forward Luis Díaz smashed in Bayern’s second off the underside of the bar.

In a recent development, just as the game appeared to be out of reach for Aston Villa, who had struggled to create much going forward for most of the game, Unai Emery’s side demonstrated some life late on. Summer signing João Gomes’s goal from the edge of the box gave them hope before Tammy Abraham nearly brought them back onto level terms, only to be denied by a fine save from 40-year-old Manuel Neuer.

Aston Villa are next in action in six days’ time when they take on Paris St-Germain in the Uefa Super Cup before kicking off their Premier League campaign at Brighton. Bayern have one more friendly to come against RB Leipzig before the DFL-Supercup against Borussia Dortmund. They then kick off the defence of their Bundesliga crown against Stuttgart at home on August 28.

Stepping up in the big moments! 🐐🧤 pic.twitter.com/r14rF39XpR.

Unai Emery’s men head home from the Far East to face PSG in the Uefa Super Cup in Salzburg next week and then have one more pre-season friendly against Borussia Monchengladbach before starting their Premier League campaign at Brighton.

Possession: Aston Villa 44%-56% Bayern MunichShots: 8-16Shots on target: 3-8Corners: 3-7.

Bizot nearly has a calamitous moment coming out of his penalty area but gets away with it.

The final whistle is blown soon after and Bayern hold on to beat Villa 2-1 in Hong Kong. They had looked comfortable when Diaz put them 2-0 up but Villa kept going until the end.

Industry observers note that victory in the final match of the #AudiFCBTour! 💪🔥 pic.twitter.com/UFhQhme62i.

The space opens up for Palhinha to shoot from range but Bizot makes a fairly comfortable save down to his right.

It was all Bayern for 80 minutes of this game but Villa have come to life in the closing stages, with Vincent Kompany’s side now holding on a bit.

There will be four added minutes.

Recent findings suggest that when Diaz scored Bayern’s second goal, Aston Villa were out of this game but it has been all Villa since then. They look the more likely to get a goal.

Recent findings suggest that gomes’ free-kick out on the left is parried behind by Neuer for a Villa corner on the right. The corner comes to nothing.

Recent findings suggest that for 80 minutes, Aston Villa barely looked like scoring but come so close to getting two goals in just a few minutes. Abraham meets a cross from the right and must think he has scored but his header is brilliantly saved by the 40-year-old Neuer.

In a recent development, maybe this game is not quite done and dusted yet. A cross from the right picks out Gomes on the edge of the box. The Brazilian takes one touch before toe poking past Neuer and into the Bayern net. Gomes meant that finish and Villa have some hope.

Abraham should have done better there. He has the space to drive down Villa’s right and has a decision to make; cross the ball to his left and drive forward himself to shoot. He takes a while to make the decision before his attempted cross is intercepted by Ito.

Boey’s yellow card was his final act of the game as he is replaced by Della Rovere. Boey did seem to be struggling with some cramp.

Bayern receive their second yellow card of the game as Boey is booked for cynically pulling down Lynch.

Cash, Maatsen and Buendia have gone off for Aston Villa.

Double substitution from Bayern as Pavic and Assomo replace Tah and Brown.

It has been revealed that A fantastic goal to put the Germans 2-0 up and it is nothing more than they deserve. Ibrahimovic finds Diaz in space on the left and the Colombian drives at Cash. As he enters the Villa box, Diaz cuts inside onto his preferred right foot and smashes a shot towards goal. It appeared to go right over Bizot, who opts not to put a hand up. The ball crashes off the underside of the bar and goes in. It has been all Bayern in this second half and that goal had been coming.

Industry observers note that bayern are knocking on the door and come very close to doubling their lead. Diaz’s shot from the edge of the box looks destined to hit the net with Bizot beaten but fortunately for Villa Abraham is on hand on his own goal line to make the block.

In a recent development, bizot makes another great save. Bayern win a free-kick out on the right after Brown was fouled. Bischoff opts to shoot instead of crossing and nearly beats Bizot at his near post but the Aston Villa keeper gets across to his left to make the save.

In a recent development, unai Emery makes a double substitution as Mings and Lynch replace Torres and Guessand. Mings takes the captain’s armband.

Industry observers note that that is a fantastic double save from Bizot, first denying Stanisic and then Ibrahimovic. Both of those shots came through bodies so Bizot did a good job of reacting and making the saves with his legs on both occasions.

It is safe to say the Bayern fans out in Hong Kong love Diaz, who is cheered every time he touches the ball.

According to recent reports, vincent Kompany is going to make a triple change as Ito, Diaz and Palhinha come on. Former Liverpool man Diaz received a great ovation from the fans in Hong Kong. Palhinha, who spent last season on loan at Tottenha, has been linked with a move to Aston Villa in this window.

Sources indicate that should Bayern have been awarded a penalty there? A ball is played in behind the Villa defence into the penalty area and Ibrahimovic appeared to be brought down but the referee waves those appeals away. On first viewing, that appeared to be a penalty.

It has been revealed that just before the hour mark, it is time for some changes from Aston Villa. Abraham and Bogarde come on for Madjo and Kamara. This is Abraham’s first appearance of this pre-season.

Good play from Gomes earns Aston Villa a free-kick not far outside the Bayern penalty area out on the left, in a similar position to the free-kick that Bayern scored from in the first half. Buendia clips in a good ball to the back post, where Guessand looks likely to score but instead misses the ball on the stretch. Should Guessand have done better with that? Probably.

Brown was starting in his customary left-back position for Bayern in the first half but is now operating out on the right wing.

Gomes leaves one late on Pavlovic and, had this been a competitive fixture, I suspect that might have been a yellow card.

It has been revealed that tah is brought down by Gomes and Bayern will have a free-kick out on the right not a million miles outside the Villa penalty area. The delivery though is poor and easily cleared away.

Sources indicate that bayern have brought Stanisic on at half-time for Laimer. Aston Villa have not made a change at the break.

We are back under way in Hong Kong.

Possession: Aston Villa 45%-55% Bayern MunichShots: 4-7Shots on target: 1-2Corners: 1-2.

The first half in Hong Kong is brought to an end and Bayern take a 1-0 lead into the break courtesy of Kim’s goal.

There will be one added minute at the end of this first half.

Aston Villa have struggled to create much going forward and have not really had a genuine goal-scoring opportunity in this first half. Their forward line though will look quite different when they kick off the seaosn than it does today.

The German side take the lead in Hong Kong. Bischof’s left-footed delivery from a free-kick out on the left is sublime, whipping it right into the corridor of uncertainty. The quality of delivery means it is quite a simple header for Kim, who makes no mistake with his header into the far corner. Kim might have been offside but obviously there is no VAR in use today. 1-0 Bayern.

That is a waste in the end from Bayern. Boey fires a pass in-field into Laimer, who takes a fantastic first touch on the turn inside the Villa half. He drives through the Villa half and at the penalty area but his pass outside looking for Cardozo is poor and overhit, with the ball rolling out for a goal kick. Laimer will be annoyed at himself having done all the hard work and then failed to execute the easy part.

Recent findings suggest that bischof eyes one up from range and tries to pick out the top corner. Bizot is routed to his spot and is hoping the shot goes wide. Bischof’s effort is always curling wide, much to Bizot’s relief.

Sources indicate that the first booking of the game goes the way of Bayern Munich. Guessand drives forward into the Bayern half and is brought down by a cynical foul from Cardozo. You were half expecting Cardozo to perhaps escape without a booking with it being a pre-season friendly but he does not. It was the right call to book him.

That was lovely from Pavlovic. The German midfielder shows good feet to beat Gomes before getting his shot away from a central position just outside the box. He forces Bizot into a decent save but one he should be making.

Sources indicate that bayern force Villa into an error and win themselves a corner as a result out on the left. It is delivered into a dangerous area at the front post but Villa do a good job of handling it and clearing their lines.

Bayern Munich have made two signings this summer; Brown from Bundesliga rivals Frankfurt and Saibari from PSV. Brown is starting at left-back for Bayern today with Saibari not involved as he closes in on a return from a knock picked up at the World Cup with Morocco. Brown feels like such a Bayern signing, nabbing a good player from a Bundesliga rival.

Aston Villa have made four signings so far this summer but just one is in their starting XI today in the form of Gomes, who joined from Midlands rivals Wolves this summer. Young Swiss midfielder Manzambi has joined from Freiburg but is at the moment out injured. Garnacho picked up a knock and Cisse, who has arrived from LASK, is not involved for Villa today.

The ball is played in behind the Aston Villa defence to pick out the run of Binder. On the edge of the Villa box, Binder gets the first touch but Lindelof is calm in defence and heads back to his keeper Bizot.

Moments later, Gomes is dispossessed inside his own half and Ibrahimovic has a shot from just outside the box but drags it wide of the far post.

Good work from 17-year-old Madjo down Aston Villa’s left wins them their first corner of the game. Buendia’s inswinger is headed away too easily at the near post. Aston Villa have seen their former set-piece coach Austin MacPhee nabbed this summer by Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea.

The referee is allowing the game to flow and thus not blowing for soft fouls.

The first chance of the game falls to Bayern Munich. Brown’s cross from the left is headed by Maatsen straight to Ibrahimovic on the edge of the box. Ibrahimovic, not any relation to Zlatan, takes the shot on first time but it is blocked by Maatsen, who makes up for that poor header with the block. The ball goes behind for a corner, which comes to nothing.

Interestingly, there are only eight outfield substitutions on the Aston Villa bench for this game, with the likes of Garnacho and McGinn picking up knocks the other day. It appears then that at least a couple of Villa outfield players will have to play the full 90.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel, Aston Villa led out by Matty Cash and Bayern Munich by Manuel Neuer, and we are closing in on kick-off in Hong Kong. A group of delegates shake the hands of both starting XIs.

According to recent reports, chelsea and Juventus played in this stadium the other night and it is safe to say that the pitch does not look in the best state ahead of kick-off today. It looks like it will continue to rip up and the last thing the two managers will want is to pick up any serious injuries.

Industry observers note that currently, before the two sides emerge, the crowd in Hong Kong are being treated to some pre-match dancing and entertainment, which includes people dressed as pandas and sharks dancing. Would the Premier League ever take inspiration and have dancing pandas before kick-off?

The likes of Ollie Watkins, Ezri Konsa and Emi Martinez are yet to return to training after their World Cup exploits and Aston Villa are also without captain John McGinn and newly introduced signing Alejandro Garnacho, who picked up knocks in their win over BG Pathum the other day.

According to recent reports, aston Villa have already sold Youri Tielemans and Morgan Rogers this summer, with Lucas Digne on the verge of a move to PSG, but could another starter be on the way out of Villa Park? England defender Ezri Konsa has been linked with moves to the likes of Arsenal and Liverpool but will Unai Emery be able to keep hold of the 28-year-old?

Joao Palhinha, who is on the bench for Bayern Munich today, has been linked with a move to Aston Villa.

It has been revealed that “Aston Villa are a top side with a very good coach. They have a large squad and will field plenty of talent. They have already played more friendlies than us, but for us it is a good challenge. It is a match in which we will learn a lot about our team’s fitness. It will be a good match for us.”.

Industry observers note that aston Villa’s preparations for the upcoming season continue out in Hong Kong as they take on Bundesliga champions Bayern Munich at the Kai Tak Stadium. These sides have met twice before; Aston Villa beat Bayern 1-0 to win the European Cup in 1981/82 before then meeting in the Champions League group stages during the 2024/25 season, with Jhon Duran’s long-range screamer giving Aston Villa a 1-0 win at Villa Park.

In a recent development, after losing two of their first three pre-season friendlies, Aston Villa have won their first two games on Asian soil and this game marks the end of their tour of the Far East. It has been a summer of significant change at Aston Villa thus far with some key members of their squad departing and some upcoming faces arriving. Youri Tielemans has departed after Manchester United triggered his release clause and they then sold Morgan Rogers to Chelsea for a British transfer record £117m. Unai Emery’s side have brought in 20-year-old Swiss midfielder Johan Manzambi, Brazilian midfielder Joao Gomes and Alejandro Garnacho, with the deal for Garnacho being an initial loan. Manzambi is right now on the sidelines due to a knee injury.

Unai Emery’s side were dealt a blow during the World Cup as Belgian midfielder Amadou Onana picked up a serious knee injury. They were though boosted by the return of Boubacar Kamara after seven months out as he scored in the 3-1 friendly victory over BG Parthum. As one midfielder returned from injury in that game, another picked up a fresh injury as John McGinn suffered a knock to his knee. The likes of Ollie Watkins, Ezri Konsa and Emi Martinez are yet to return after their world Cup exploits. They begin their Premier League campaign with an away game on the south coast against Brighton on August 23 but will be involved in the Uefa Super Cup against PSG next week having lifted the Europa League last season.

According to recent reports, bayern Munich head into this season looking to win a third straight Bundesliga title and have won two of their three friendlies, losing once. They have added Moroccan attacker Ismael Saibari from PSV and German left-back Nathaniel Brown from Bundesliga rivals Eintracht Frankfurt to their ranks this summer. The likes of Harry Kane, Dayot Upamecano and Michael Olise are not available as they are still yet to return after World Cup duty but Vincent Kompany has confirmed that Bayern’s German stars are set to return.

Industry observers note that after today, Bayern have one more friendly against RB Leipzig before the DFL-Supercup against Borussia Dortmund. They then kick off the defence of their Bundesliga crown against Stuttgart at home on August 28.

US curbs China’s remote access to AI chips through overseas data centres

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (557 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thenextweb

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the US Commerce Department on Monday moved to stop Chinese companies from renting American AI chips through data centres in other countries.
  • In a recent development, the rule has two main parts, according to its text.
  • It has been revealed that second, exporters now need a licence to ship advanced chips to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the US Commerce Department on Monday moved to stop Chinese companies from renting American AI chips through data centres in other countries. Its Bureau of Industry and Security issued an interim final rule on remote access to advanced chips and servers. The bureau remarked the rule was “written by and at the direction of” the Treasury Department and the National Security Council.

In a recent development, the rule has two main parts, according to its text. First, suppliers now need a licence for any data centre, anywhere, that serves companies headquartered in China, Macau or the other countries in the US’s D:5 group. The threshold is more than 12 million units of “aggregate TPP”, a measure of computing power. Data centres already serving such customers have 90 days from the rule’s start to get a licence.

It has been revealed that second, exporters now need a licence to ship advanced chips to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil. The rule calls them countries with “a higher-than-normal risk of diversion”. Companies headquartered in the US are exempt, as long as they file monthly reports.

Industry observers note that recommendation systems used by online shops and social media companies are also exempt. The rule takes effect once it appears in the Federal Register, and the public then has 60 days to comment.

Industry observers note that the rule also tightens checks on chip foundries and packagers that make advanced chips for designers in the countries now facing a licence. It formally scraps the Biden administration’s AI Diffusion Rule. The government never enforced that rule, and the bureau said in May 2025 that it would rescind it.

Commerce said it would watch for countries that tolerate evasion. Possible penalties include import restrictions, fresh licence rules and Entity List designations, according to the rule.

In a recent development, the move follows Jensen Huang’s resignation as Nvidia CEO last week, after he admitted an affair with Alice Huang. She is a former executive of Megaspeed, a Singapore manufacturer that US officials suspect of passing Nvidia chips to China. Megaspeed has denied wrongdoing. In June, Commerce had already moved against Chinese firms’ overseas units buying the chips directly.

Nvidia shares fell as much as 2.9% on Monday. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropped as much as 5.5%, Maggie Eastland and Magan Crane reported for Bloomberg.

Recent findings suggest that in a post on X, Chris McGuire of the Council on Foreign Relations called the rule “a major step forward”, CNBC reported. He noted loopholes remain, including some covering activity inside the US.

“I have never seen a BIS rule that was not written by BIS,” McGuire wrote.

Analysts told Fortune that the rule could hit Southeast Asian countries that want to host data centres for Chinese firms.

“For Malaysia, the controls could be disastrous,” Joshua Kurlantzick, a senior fellow at the Council on Foreign Relations, told Fortune.

According to recent reports, on Monday, before leaving for Asia, Donald Trump said he had no intends to replace Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, Bloomberg reported. Lutnick faces criticism from lawmakers and Treasury over enforcement. Trump meets Xi Jinping on Thursday in Shenzhen.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that crypto exchange Binance has warned iPhone users about an iOS vulnerability that could allow malicious apps to access sensitive data stored by other apps.
  • In a post published on X (via AppleInsider), Binance notes that a vulnerability called worse_query could allow “malicious apps to read local files from other apps, putting seed phrases, private keys, and login credentials at risk across the entire ecosystem.”.
  • Binance claims the flaw affects iOS 26.7.1, iOS 27.0.1, and iOS 27.2.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that crypto exchange Binance has warned iPhone users about an iOS vulnerability that could allow malicious apps to access sensitive data stored by other apps. Here are the details.

In a post published on X (via AppleInsider), Binance notes that a vulnerability called worse_query could allow “malicious apps to read local files from other apps, putting seed phrases, private keys, and login credentials at risk across the entire ecosystem.”.

Binance claims the flaw affects iOS 26.7.1, iOS 27.0.1, and iOS 27.2. However, a Community Note points out that researchers describe the vulnerability as an unpatched zero-day and that Apple’s latest security updates, including iOS 27.2.1 (the current version at the time of writing), do not mention a fix.

It has been revealed that A vulnerability (worse_query) affecting iOS 26.7.1, 27.0.1, and 27.2 allows malicious apps to read local files from other apps, putting seed phrases, private keys, and login credentials at risk across the entire ecosystem. This is an iOS-level matter, not unique to Binance.….

That said, in addition to updating their devices, Binance recommends that iPhone crypto holders take the following immediate actions:.

The vulnerability was disclosed by security researchers @0xjohnny and @forcequitOS, who published a proof of concept on GitHub demonstrating how it can be used to bypass iOS sandbox protections, which normally prevent apps from accessing each other’s files.

Researcher @forcequitOS also noted that neither iOS 27.2.1 nor iOS 27.3 beta 1 patches the vulnerability.

In a recent development, just as a general statement so there isn’t any confusion about it, worse_query is *not* patched in iOS 27.2.1 and 27.3 beta 1. I’ll update version support on the readme when it’s patched.

Although the researcher describes the code as intended for developers and not useful on its own, other developers have already built apps using it, including a file manager that can access, modify, and delete data belonging to other apps without requiring a jailbreak.

According to The Hacker News, neither Binance nor the researchers have reported any attacks or cryptocurrency thefts involving the vulnerability so far.

#4060. Latest Update: iPhone Duo one week later: The future, or not for me?

Latest Update: iPhone Duo one week later: The future, or not for me?

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (763 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • My iPhone Duo arrived last Thursday, so I’ve had a week to use it as my daily carry.
  • After a week using the iPhone Duo, in some ways I have a lot of clarity about the product, and in other ways my thinking is very clouded.
  • To put it simply: I’m not having a great time with the Duo, which makes me wonder if the problem is me, not it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

My iPhone Duo arrived last Thursday, so I’ve had a week to use it as my daily carry. My early experience has been mixed, so I keep asking myself an important question: is this the iPhone’s future and I just need to adapt, or is the Duo simply not for everyone?

After a week using the iPhone Duo, in some ways I have a lot of clarity about the product, and in other ways my thinking is very clouded.

To put it simply: I’m not having a great time with the Duo, which makes me wonder if the problem is me, not it.

I’ve seen countless social media posts from Duo owners proclaiming how much they love the product. And I absolutely believe them. The iPhone Duo is a remarkable innovation for the iPhone. It’s cool, weird, and wonderful in all sorts of ways. But for me and my needs (preferences?), it’s been more frustrating than enjoyable.

And that frustration mainly boils down to one thing: I almost never want to open it.

According to recent reports, I’d estimate at least 90% of my iPhone Duo usage involves the front display. And when I unfold it the remaining 10% of the time, it’s often because I force myself to do it in the hopes of discovering what I’m missing out on. Like, I know I should be unfolding it more, so I do. But it doesn’t add any real value for me.

Because I rarely want to open the iPhone Duo, I’m left using the outer display all the time. In that mode, the Duo is too heavy for extended use, too wide to comfortably reach, and the UI in most apps is an adjustment.

Are these dealbreakers? No. I could live with the Duo’s outer display if I had to, but it’s definitely an inferior experience to my iPhone 18 Pro.

If I was opening the iPhone Duo more, and actually taking advantage of the key value proposition of foldables—that you can unfold them—I doubt the outer screen would bother me much.

But what I’ve found, at least so far, is that one-handed iPhone use is very crucial to me, which rules out using the inner display. I use my iPhone mostly for quick interactions, and often with a child in one hand (I have three very young kids). In situations when I do have two hands free to open the Duo, I’m probably sitting in front of my iPad Pro with a Magic Keyboard attached and would rather use the iPad instead.

So again: is the problem with the Duo, or with me?

I think foldables and slab phones will obviously coexist as there will be fans of each.

I’m absolutely already converted however and am loving my duo.

It has been revealed that considering the Air was my favourite phone up until this it’s surprised me. I love proper one handed use again on the outside screen and unfolded it’s much nicer than my old mini 7.

I get it’s not for everyone but those that click with it like myself have a superb device!

Recent findings suggest that I think it’s the latter, but I’m not sure “problem” is the right word. I just don’t find myself using it the way it’s meant to be used. And that’s fine.

Sources indicate that I want to love the iPhone Duo, because I see how much fun other people are having with it. And maybe given more time, something will click and I’ll start to use it “as intended.”.

If iPhone Duo is the future of the iPhone, I’ll adapt and move on with my life. But one week in, I think it’s probably just not for me. And if it’s not for me, maybe there are a lot of people who will continue preferring non-foldable iPhones for many years to come.

What’s your iPhone Duo experience been like? Are you loving it or struggling? Let us know in the comments.

Recent findings suggest that inside, one of the best home security cameras not only can warn you if someone gets into your house, but can also be used to keep tabs on your pets while you're away. Since all cameras have built-in speakers, you could even shoo them off the couch if they're not supposed to sleep there.

Plus, the camera can pan and tilt, letting you track things more easily. And, the solar panel means you might never have to plug it in.

Looking for something a little cheaper? Blink's cameras offer excellent 2K resolution, and thanks to their innovative tech, can last up to two years without needing to replace their batteries. This deal gets you two cameras for 66% off.

Industry observers note that the best video doorbells of course let you know who's knocking, but the models we like the most also have features such as package detection, so you know when UPS or FedEx has delivered something to your door. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, in an update rolling out today, Gentler Streak is introducing upcoming ways for consumers to track their wellbeing and personalize the app’s guidance based on how they feel.
  • One of my favorite exercise-tracking apps got even better today with an update that expands its functionality beyond workouts and fitness metrics to better reflect how users actually feel.
  • Starting today, Gentler Streak will let owners log how they feel each day, including their mood, symptoms, and other factors that may not be reflected in their health and fitness data.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, in an update rolling out today, Gentler Streak is introducing upcoming ways for consumers to track their wellbeing and personalize the app’s guidance based on how they feel. Here are the details.

One of my favorite exercise-tracking apps got even better today with an update that expands its functionality beyond workouts and fitness metrics to better reflect how users actually feel.

Starting today, Gentler Streak will let owners log how they feel each day, including their mood, symptoms, and other factors that may not be reflected in their health and fitness data.

Some days, the way we feel isn’t reflected in what the data says, no matter the data quality. “How I Feel” captures the part that devices can’t grasp: personal context. And how you feel is not only a mood: it is also a sore throat, heavy legs or a poor night’s sleep. The feature was inspired by the Gentler Streak community, including people living with chronic fatigue, fibromyalgia, ADHD, and those not wearing their Apple Watch at night. Without overnight signals, their guidance has less to work with.

According to the team behind Gentler Streak, these newly introduced features are aimed at users whose health and fitness data may not accurately reflect how they feel, including those dealing with chronic conditions, menopause, stress, or poor sleep.

In practice, the app will now feature four tabs: Today, Health, Workouts, and Insights. In the Today and Health tabs, a new “Anything to add?” field will let consumers rate how they feel, from Great to Off, and add context about what might be affecting their well-being, including fatigue, feeling calm, or custom tags.

You decide when the prompt appears. Go to Profile > Settings > Self-Evaluation Prompt and choose one of three options: only when your vitals or sleep are off, always on, or never.

Gentler Stories notes that the self-assessments will override the app’s wellbeing estimates for that day, with its daily guidance adjusting accordingly.

The Today tab will also feature an expanded 10- or 30-day timeline showing logged workouts, wellbeing estimates, potential symptoms, poor sleep or vitals, and the first day of a menstrual period, while Health will introduce an interactive chart showing people how their wellbeing changes over time, with the ability to filter by symptoms.

People can now also customize which information appears on their Today screen, including vitals, sleep, steps, menstrual cycle, VO₂ max, and workouts, which is a nice touch.

For people who are sick, injured, or taking a break from exercise, the app’s hallmark Activity Path will make way for a new Wellbeing Path, which lets them track their wellbeing on a daily basis.

Recent findings suggest that for customers with Active status, a new colorful wellbeing line will appear beneath the Activity Path, reflecting how they feel each day. This information is logged automatically for those who wear their Apple Watch overnight, or based on self-assessments for those who don’t.

Importantly, Gentler Stories notes that all information entered through the latest feature remains on the user’s device, with no accounts or manufacturer-operated servers involved.

Gentler Streak is available for free on the App Store, with in-app purchases for monthly, yearly, family, and lifetime subscriptions.

  • Nvidia’s board is not considering bringing Jensen Huang back as chief executive, a person familiar with the matter told CNBC on Monday.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jensen Huang at the White House AI Summit at the Andrew W. Mellon Auditorium in Washington, D.C., 23 July 2025.

Nvidia’s board is not considering bringing Jensen Huang back as chief executive, a person familiar with the matter told CNBC on Monday. The report came hours after President Donald Trump remarked he “would not mind” Jensen Huang’s return.

Industry observers note that the board’s focus is its investigation into Huang, and it is not in talks to bring him back, the person told CNBC’s Seema Mody and Kif Leswing. Nvidia has hired the law firm Wachtell Lipton to lead the board’s investigation. It is looking at whether Huang’s conduct put national security or Nvidia’s secrets at risk.

On Friday, a representative for the board mentioned it was choosing a search firm to find a latest chief executive, CNBC reported. Huang resigned last week, after 33 years running the manufacturer he founded.

According to recent reports, trump spoke to reporters on Monday as he left the White House for the Philippines and China, the Fresh York Post’s Emily Goodin reported. A reporter asked him about a Financial Times report that Huang had discussed a return with allies. Trump stated Huang had “learned a big lesson”.

“I guess maybe one lesson is more important than another, but I would certainly not mind seeing that,” Trump said.

Sources indicate that reporters also asked about Alice Huang, the Megaspeed executive whom US officials suspect of working for Chinese intelligence. She and Jensen Huang share a surname but no family ties.

Sources indicate that “I don’t know that she’s a spy at all. Nobody’s proven that,” Trump noted.

Asked whether national security had been put at risk, Trump answered as CNBC reported:.

“It was not put at risk, and our country is now stronger than ever before.”.

In a recent development, no one has charged Alice Huang with any wrongdoing, and China has denied the allegations, the Post reported. Megaspeed has said she left the manufacturer in August 2025.

Trump stated he did not expect to raise Huang or chip sales when he meets Chinese President Xi Jinping.

“We’re heading to China, and I don’t think you want to insult China just before you get there,” he said.

It has been revealed that an online petition to reinstate Huang has drawn 180,000 signatures, CNBC reported. Elon Musk, Y Combinator chief executive Garry Tan and Epic Games chief executive Tim Sweeney have backed it.

Altimeter Capital’s Brad Gerstner told CNBC on Monday that Huang had not discussed a comeback with him. A representative for Huang declined to comment on the speculation on Sunday, according to CNBC.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A poll of 9to5Mac readers who were lucky enough to take delivery of their iPhone Duo in the first few days indicates that 30% of them have returned it for a refund.

While that could be considered bad news for the future of the device, I don’t personally consider it either surprising or worrying ….

Following a report by The Verge on iPhone Duo buyers who opted to return the device for a refund within Apple’s 14-day “no questions asked” period, we thought it would be interesting to get a sense of how many people may have done this.

9to5Mac readers were always likely to have had their fingers hovering over the pre-order button for the best shot at taking early delivery, with the first of these having hit the end of the 14-day window. We ask those of you who fall into this category to tell us whether you kept or returned the device.

With close to 6,000 total votes, the results revealed that close to a third of you returned your Duo.

For any other device, that would be a disastrous return rate. For the Duo, however, I don’t think it’s terribly surprising.

I voted to say I returned it just so I could see the results. I’ve never ordered nor returned an iPhone Duo.

Not providing a way to see the results without voting will have massively skewed the results. Even if the poll were better, this is a wild claim to draw from one specific, poorly assembled assembled poll.

As we noted yesterday, Apple described the iPhone Duo as “the most transformational change to iPhone since the original.” The size of that change shows up in a whole range of ways, from the weight of the device through the changed aspect ratio of the front display to a completely new way of using an iPhone.

Recent findings suggest that throw in the extremely high price tag, and I’ve always suspected that a significant number of iPhone Duo buyers would be viewing it as an experiment rather than a committed purchase. Our own Ryan Christoffel is an example of that “try it and see” attitude. One week in, he’s reached an interim conclusion that it’s probably not for him.

For those who’ve decided to return it, a number of readers shared their reasons.

“Returned it – I can’t go back to Touch ID.”.

It has been revealed that “Returned it. Cameras are key for me.”.

“I want to like it, but I just can’t get there. It’s awkward, and the outside screen is way too small.”.

“Returned it. Not for me. I do not want to open the phone every time I want a larger screen and Apple made the outer display much less usable than it should be with that silly permanent dock. I also use my phones left-handed.”.

“During a vacation in Morocco, we spent a night camping in the Sahara Desert. I was extremely careful with the phone and tried to avoid using it in the sand altogether. However, on the second day, when I opened it inside the tent, I heard a crunching sound coming from the hinge. Sand had somehow gotten inside. I tried everything I could to clean it, but nothing worked. The inner display was still functioning perfectly, but the phone would no longer open all the way. Even worse, when I tried to close it, I had to force it shut.”.

For me personally, it couldn’t be my only phone, given the priority I place on the device as a camera, but I am still lusting after it. Given the continued extended delivery times – with random checks showing shipping in late January – I don’t think Apple has much to worry about here.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that openAI is expanding its ChatGPT for Academic Researchers programme with 50,000 fresh grants, each covering up to three people, and now aims to reach 200,000 researchers.
  • OpenAI will give 50,000 more free ChatGPT grants to academic researchers, the firm confirmed on Monday.
  • According to recent reports, there is a catch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that openAI is expanding its ChatGPT for Academic Researchers programme with 50,000 fresh grants, each covering up to three people, and now aims to reach 200,000 researchers. New grants get ChatGPT Plus instead of Pro, and go to the first eligible applicants rather than by lottery.

OpenAI will give 50,000 more free ChatGPT grants to academic researchers, the firm confirmed on Monday. Applications open on November 23, and grants go to the first eligible applicants instead of by lottery. Each grant covers a researcher and up to two collaborators, or up to 150,000 people in total.

According to recent reports, there is a catch. Researchers in the pilot got ChatGPT Pro, OpenAI’s top tier, while latest grants come with the cheaper Plus plan. OpenAI claims most pilot users would have stayed within Plus limits, and the switch lets it reach more teams.

OpenAI now aims to reach 200,000 researchers, double the goal it set when the pilot debuted in July. Back then, each researcher could invite up to four collaborators. So far, 20,000 researchers in 33 countries have joined.

According to recent reports, openAI also published a study of how more than 1,800 scientists used ChatGPT in the pilot. On average, reading and learning made up 28% of their science messages, and writing 27%. Surveyed participants stated the same work would have taken nearly twice as long without AI.

That figure is self-reported, and OpenAI indicates the study does not prove AI speeds up discovery. It also names funding, staff and lab capacity as limits on testing new ideas.

Sources indicate that the grants are one of several OpenAI science pushes. It offers free seats on GPT-Rosalind, its biology model, to US university labs, and gave $5M to a Simons Foundation effort to help mathematicians check AI results. In August, its unreleased Astra model claimed to have solved ten open problems in maths.

According to recent reports, rivals are courting scientists too. Anthropic introduced Claude Science, an AI workbench for labs, in June. Google DeepMind opened its science models to 200 European researchers in October.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, most days Iâm in the terminal cdâing into directories and opening files in my editor.
  • Recent findings suggest that so I made psychic, a fast terminal-based file browser.
  • Everything about how it works flows from a key design decision: it has to be fast enough to enhancement within one frame after a keypress.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, most days Iâm in the terminal cdâing into directories and opening files in my editor. In any given week itâs mostly the same files and dirs because Iâm working on the same projects. I was annoyed I had to remember where files live, and tired of tab-completing the same few paths. My computer should already know which file I want to open!

Recent findings suggest that so I made psychic, a fast terminal-based file browser. It tracks the directories you go to and remembers which files you open. It trains a lightweight ML model on your data and ranks results using that model. It prioritizes interactivity and speed above all else: results update as you type and the UI renders in under 16ms.

Everything about how it works flows from a key design decision: it has to be fast enough to enhancement within one frame after a keypress. Iâd rather do 10 fast searches in the space of a couple seconds, than 1 smart search that takes many seconds to complete.

I use psychic every time Iâm on my computer. Itâs become the main way I move around the filesystem. Some numbers: Since I started using it in October 2025,.

(These are from the built-in psychic stats command, which you can run on your own history!).

Itâs on homebrew: brew install kshitijl/tap/psychic.

In a recent development, on the left are search results. On the right is a preview of the file or directory currently selected. You type a query in the bottom and the results are filtered and ranked, changing with every letter. If you hit Enter on a file, it opens your terminal editor in the same window and waits in the background. If itâs a directory, it restarts the search from inside there. It remembers every file and dir you open, and a shell integration records every dir you cd into from outside psychic. All of those are included in every search.

Itâs like fzf and zoxide had a baby, plus a small ML model that learns your patterns and favorites. Itâs doing ad optimization on your own data, to help you navigate your computer faster.

All your searches and clicks get written to a sqlite db on your computer. psychic trains a LightGBM model on that data. The model learns to predict which files youâll open, based on your search query. psychic uses the model to rank search results. After every keypress, psychic reruns the model and reranks all results.

For more details, see the README in the repo.

According to recent reports, the model I use is LightGBM, an implementation of gradient-boosted trees. Itâs tiny and fast and trains in seconds. It can learn rules that depend on threshold values. For example, it can learn a rule like âFiles above 1 MB are only opened if theyâve been modified in the last 24 hoursâ, like log files. LightGBM also has the excellent LambdaRank objective, which is specialized for exactly this kind of ranking task.

Industry observers note that the latency budget ruled out any model thatâs not local: a network call could easily be over 10 ms or worse. It also ruled out LLMs or any kind of transformer model. Linear and logistic regression were too simple and performed much worse than LightGBM.

The model is re-trained from scratch every time you open psychic. This means it always reflects your current usage patterns. Training happens in the background and writes the model to disk when itâs done. We donât switch to using the new model while youâre looking at results, because itâs jarring when apps do that. Instead, we wait for when youâre not looking at the screen, like when youâre opening a file in an editor or when you click on a directory. Then we switch to the new model. Iâm proud of this careful little dance.

When a user has just started using psychic, there arenât enough clicks to train on. We use a simple model that rewards recent clicks, recent modification time and a fuzzy match between the query and filename. The final score is a weighted sum of the simple model and ML model. With few clicks, the simple model dominates. As more clicks accumulate, the ML modelâs score gets higher weight, until itâs basically 1.

Sources indicate that I use a carefully chosen set of features to try to predict which file youâll open. Some features are simple: how recently you last clicked it within psychic, its modification time, whether the filename starts with the query, a fuzzy text match score between the query and the filename. Hereâs a debug pane that shows the features and some performance stats:.

According to recent reports, this debug pane was very helpful in the beginning for figuring out weird results or slowness. These days psychic is pretty stable but I still like opening it sometimes.

Sources indicate that one feature is ânumber of recent clicks on files that are in the same directory as this oneâ. This feature helps the model boost files that are in right now active projects.

It has been revealed that the feature âclicks for this queryâ helps the model associate specific queries with specific files, without having to literally remember filenames and query texts. This way, while the model doesnât directly see filenames, it can still remember associations.

Every training run writes a pdf with some stats. Here we see a training curve and the gain of each feature.

An episode is defined as everything that happens from opening psychic (or from the last click) to clicking on an item. So a single episode has a bunch of queries, including hitting backspace and trying new queries. The feature âengagements in episode with queryâ counts the number of times you clicked on a file at any point in an episode that had the current query. So if you always type âesâ and end up clicking on âbayesian-estimate.mdâ, then the model can see that association. Next time you type âesâ, the model will put that file at the top of the list.

According to recent reports, here are SHAP values and a dot chart. These help me understand how much a feature affects the modelâs output, and to interpret why a model behaves the way it does. For example, the dot chart shows that the model prefers recently modified files, and dislikes most massive files.

Recent findings suggest that I watch perf closely and spent a lot of effort on a good benchmarking setup, plus perf logging. Every commit has performance benchmarks. If you use psychic and get bad performance, thatâs a bug! Let me know and Iâll fix it.

It has been revealed that my tech choices were driven by performance. Probably the most vital choices were Rust and LightGBM.

Syscalls are expensive but of course this whole program is syscalls. I tried to minimize syscalls. No filesystem syscalls in the main render loop; I carefully made sure that we ask for file metadata at the time we walk the filesystem and then carry that around everywhere else.

Stanford professors’ AI lab Noeri releases with $110m, backed by Nvidia

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (513 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thenextweb

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Yejin Choi (left) and Carlos Guestrin, co-founders and co-CEOs of Noeri.
  • Noeri, an AI lab founded this year by Stanford professors Yejin Choi and Carlos Guestrin, has raised $110m, the firm revealed on Monday.
  • Bloomberg’s Dina Bass first reported the round earlier on Monday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Yejin Choi (left) and Carlos Guestrin, co-founders and co-CEOs of Noeri.

Noeri, an AI lab founded this year by Stanford professors Yejin Choi and Carlos Guestrin, has raised $110m, the firm revealed on Monday. Menlo Ventures led the round, with Madrona Venture Group, Kindred Ventures, Wing Venture Capital and NEA. Cisco Investments, Nvidia and Snowflake joined as strategic investors.

Bloomberg’s Dina Bass first reported the round earlier on Monday. Noeri did not disclose its valuation, Bloomberg reported.

Noeri builds self-improving AI for companies and for scientific research. It indicates most AI models stop learning once their training ends, while its systems keep improving on the job.

Its AI studies a manufacturer’s own data and workflows. It then changes the system around a task: the instructions, the tools, which model handles each step and, where it pays off, the models themselves. Each change comes with an explanation, and a person approves it, as in a code review.

The system works with closed and open-weight models. Customers keep ownership of their data and of the workflows and models they build, the company noted.

In a recent development, noeri also wants its AI to work with scientists. It would form hypotheses, run experiments and learn from the results, on problems from new molecules and proteins to complex technical systems. The company says smaller, specialised models make that kind of search affordable.

“Every company we talk to is riding the same curve: pay more for the best model, or settle for worse results from a cheaper one,” said Carlos Guestrin, co-founder and co-CEO of Noeri.

In a recent development, choi told Bloomberg the idea came partly from work with a Stanford microbiology and immunology team. The team wanted cheaper ways to use OpenAI’s models. Choi stated their small AI, which learned to use other models, beat GPT-5 on that team’s research needs.

“We made this small AI that learns to use other AI, including GPT-4, but not 5 because at Stanford we are too poor to use GPT-5 all the time for research,” Choi told Bloomberg.

Choi and Guestrin are co-CEOs. Choi is a MacArthur Fellow and a former professor at the University of Washington and senior director at the Allen Institute for AI. Bloomberg reported that she was also a distinguished scientist at Nvidia.

Guestrin co-founded Turi, the machine learning platform Apple bought in 2016, and then led Apple’s central machine learning and AI organisation. He co-created XGBoost, an open-source machine learning library. Bloomberg describes him as director of the Stanford AI Lab.

Noeri has its headquarters in Palo Alto and an office in Zurich. It is hiring researchers and engineers in both cities. It is working with partners across industries, including some of its investors. Menlo Ventures also backed Town’s $108m round in October.

“Yejin and I both have worries about centralization, about one organization owning everything,” Guestrin told Bloomberg.

Tech Report: The Active Directory Era Is Finally Over

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • “Life was simpler on Active Directory, at least I could manage every identity”.
  • I made that quote up, but there is nostalgia for a golden age of corporate IT that’s never coming back: Many enterprises still (try to) track identities in Active Directory (AD), a service that’s old enough to drink and crumbles at the scale of modern cloud computing.
  • It held up because the architecture is simple enough: Active Directory is an LDAP directory to store identities and a Kerberos implementation to let them authenticate, wrapped in decent UX and with continued updates.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

“Life was simpler on Active Directory, at least I could manage every identity”.

I made that quote up, but there is nostalgia for a golden age of corporate IT that’s never coming back: Many enterprises still (try to) track identities in Active Directory (AD), a service that’s old enough to drink and crumbles at the scale of modern cloud computing.

It held up because the architecture is simple enough: Active Directory is an LDAP directory to store identities and a Kerberos implementation to let them authenticate, wrapped in decent UX and with continued updates.

AD accomplished the goal of identity management: A way to know all identities, who vouched for them, and where they’re valid. It answered three questions in a unified catalog:.

Security policies are moot if you can't answer any one of them. I spent many hours keeping our Active Directory catalog accurate so it could answer these questions, because everything downstream depended on it: issuing certificates automatically with Certificate Services, applying settings at scale with Group Policies, and more.

There were always some compromises: databases with local users, Linux servers requiring workarounds (Thank you SSSD!), but most users and machines in my network had an identity in Active Directory, and I knew which didn’t.

Industry observers note that but unifying every identity in Active Directory (or any one directory) is nearly impossible with modern cloud architecture. There’s an AD ecosystem of security products, password rotations, and sync plugins that modernizes it, but nothing can undo architecture choices from a bygone era.

Active Directory is the newly introduced mainframe: great for its time, but you’d never choose to start from scratch. Replacing it is impossible because it’s so entrenched.

Active Directory can accurately reflect human identities with a few integrations and plugins, but machine identities are nearly impossible.

Industry observers note that maybe that’s controversial. You can come to me with torches, pitchforks, and architectural diagrams about Kubernetes pod identity attestation in AD, but Active Directory is still a piece of infrastructure built for a bygone era.

Most organizations are creating grave security risks because they don’t understand modern machine identity. I once spoke to someone at a conference who told me they had recently discovered a publicly exposed Lambda function. Bad enough, but that function’s policy was iam:* meaning it could take any IAM action, including crowning any attacker the organization’s superadmin. Oh, and by the way, this was a defense organization.

Sources indicate that if an organization with high security requirements makes these blunders, you don’t want to know what happens at other organizations. This problem isn’t specific to AD, but it is a symptom of organizations not figuring out how to correctly attest machine identity in modern software development.

To understand why no organization can account for all of its machine identities in AD, we need to understand how a machine enters a domain. A domain is an administrative boundary that shares security rules. In practice, this is usually an organization.

When a fresh machine joins your domain, three main events happen:.

Sources indicate that when that machine logs in, it authenticates to a Domain Controller (the server running Active Directory for the domain), which trusts it because the machine is in its directory. But the machine had to enter the directory first.

According to recent reports, when Active Directory was built, that meant a human manually added it. “Machines” were physical servers that got delivered to the office, installed in the server dungeon room, and registered by a human admin.

Human approval doesn’t scale to developers creating and deprecating testing databases, Kubernetes clusters, and CI runners at will. Contemporary AD implementations deal with this by deferring authority. An admin token (sometimes hardcoded…) automatically joins new identities.

Using human credentials to join fresh machines is a workaround that negates the point: Admin approval implies a human can tell you about each trusted device.

No admin can know every EC2 instance, PostgreSQL database, or CI runner in the organization. This is also because when AD was built, machine identities were long-lived devices, not ephemeral cloud resources.

Active Directory was built for human approval of long-lived infrastructure, but now often auto-approves short-lived cloud resources.

According to recent reports, even if you built all of the complex automations to reflect every testing database and Kubernetes pod in AD with automated admin approval, it’s security theater. The unified directory would exist on paper, but lack authority.

Modern cloud infrastructure automatically asserts machine identity:.

It has been revealed that these two examples have modern assumptions baked in: machines need to self-serve their identities when they’re spun up. They also assume a narrow scope.

According to recent reports, the unified directory of identity management aimed to encompass every device, user, and piece of infrastructure. Authenticating to the Domain Controller would be enough to get access to everything a user/machine needs and nothing they don’t.

According to recent reports, this is the identity perimeter: where an identity is valid. In the Active Directory era, the perimeter was as large as possible. The more complete the perimeter, the more authoritative the directory. As an example, SQL Server accepts Windows authentication (i.e. an AD identity) or SQL authentication (username and password). Active Directory admins choose Windows auth to keep the perimeter large.

Anything outside of the directory would be a “shadow identity”: a valid identity that grants access to corporate infrastructure, but isn’t accounted for in identity management (unless you consider the post-it note on my monitor identity management).

According to recent reports, A separate username-password set creates a separate perimeter. This used to be a problem, but is now the norm. Each API key, database string, or auth token creates a separate perimeter because they’re a credential that represents an identity for just one service. As an example, GitHub automation requires personal access tokens or GitHub private keys and doesn’t work with any directory identity.

But just to make it harder, zero-trust architecture makes machines constantly authenticate to each other, which skyrockets the count of credentials and creates hundreds of perimeters.

In theory, a small perimeter shrinks the blast radius of any breach: A compromised Notion session token should only give Notion access. In practice, an attacker may find additional credentials in Notion, which lets them expand their access. Oh, and the physical security layer of firewalls and physical perimeters is gone in the cloud era, so a leaked credential works from any attacker’s laptop.

Industry observers note that this should concern admins more than it does: many teams keep troves of sensitive plaintext credentials in .env files or hardcode them in configuration files. The response is often lackluster:.

A solution like Active Directory is nearly useless for solving these complications.

Organizations can tame the complexity of machine identity in the cloud, but not as simply as one massive Active Directory list. Instead, we see two main vectors to fix this:.

It has been revealed that the first is identity federation, where one platform trusts another platform’s approval to authenticate a workload. All three major clouds support this.

According to recent reports, using OpenID Connect (OIDC), AWS can sign a token for an EC2 instance to access PostgreSQL in Azure. Entra federated credentials natively support this use case and would trust the EC2 workload.

This works for many use cases. If you’re exclusively on AWS and run Terraform from GitHub Actions, OIDC federation straight into IAM does the job: You get visibility, know why you trust it, and know its scope. But it’s laborious to implement each relationship, which means it relies on IAM administrators who can barely keep up with group membership requests. Moreover, if stated pipeline is breached by, say, a supply chain attack (which are common nowadays), the whole perimeter is breached.

According to recent reports, even if your admins are bored, no cloud has native bridges between every possible tool, so federation stops as soon as any service only accepts an API key. Organizations shouldn’t accept unruly, long-standing plaintext credentials outside of security purview.

Industry observers note that that’s why organizations adopt a brokering approach. Here, credentials live in a secrets manager like Infisical (which securely stores and then delivers secrets to workloads at runtime). This creates a meta-perimeter for all of those micro-perimeters. Infisical (or another tool) acts like a broker: Machines authenticate to it, they broker access to the credential store, and inject the credentials the identity can read into its runtime.

These two patterns can bring order to the Wild West of machine identity in the cloud era. They check the boxes Active Directory once did:.

This is especially important as organizations increasingly adopt AI agents, which often need their own identities, separate security policies, and even separate security tooling. Getting machine identity right is more important than ever. If you can’t keep track of testing databases and a Stripe API key, you don’t want autonomous software that can create its own databases and send that API key to strangers online.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that jensen Huang has resigned as the CEO of Nvidia following recent reports of extramarital affairs, including one involving a woman suspected of spying for China. Here are the details.

In late October, The Upcoming York Times reported on Jensen Huang’s “close relationship” with Alice Huang, a former managing director at Singapore-based Megaspeed, whom US intelligence officials reportedly identified as a Chinese intelligence asset suspected of passing information to Beijing.

Industry observers note that according to subsequent reports, Chinese intelligence allegedly recruited her to gather information about Jensen Huang and influence his position on selling advanced AI chips to Chinese companies. China disputes the espionage allegations, dismissing them as groundless speculation intended to smear the country.

According to recent reports, that said, while Nvidia previously denied any impropriety in their relationship, Huang admitted last weekend to having an extramarital affair in a message to employees, saying, “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did.” He did not mention Alice Huang directly.

In the following days, concerns grew over the potential national security implications of the relationship, in addition to Nvidia seeing its stock plummet.

And while Huang remained CEO as Nvidia’s board commissioned an independent investigation into the allegations, The Upcoming York Times reported on Wednesday that he had a second extramarital affair, this time with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare, who reports directly to him.

According to recent reports, in the hours that followed, The Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia’s board was preparing to meet to decide Huang’s future. Soon after, Semafor reported that some board members favored Nvidia CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO, while other reports suggested that Huang’s daughter, Madison Huang, could eventually succeed him. Madison Huang works at Nvidia as senior director of product marketing.

Semafor also named Apple’s chief hardware officer, Johny Srouji, as a potential successor, while Bloomberg reported that Nvidia had hired an outside firm to identify candidates.

Now, Nvidia has officially announced that Huang “has resigned as President, Chief Executive Officer, and a member of the Board, effective immediately.”.

Recent findings suggest that the company confirmed that Kress has been appointed interim CEO, while retaining her current responsibilities, until a permanent successor is named. The company is considering both internal and external candidates.

Nvidia also announced that Harvey C. Jones, a longtime technology executive and venture investor, has been appointed the tech giant’s first-ever board chair.

In a statement, Jones stated the board has “full confidence in Colette and the leadership team,” adding that Nvidia expects its operations, customer commitments, and product roadmap to continue without interruption.

The shareholder lawsuits over the broad-spectrum mismanagement are going to be incredible.

No succession plan. Lying to investors to cover up the CEO’s unethical and foolish behavior. Having a super-weak board of directors absent anyone with high-level relevant experience.

Nvidia did not directly address the allegations surrounding Huang in its announcement, instead thanking him for his contributions to the company over the past 33 years.

Following the Times’ Wednesday report, Nvidia shares plunged in after-hours trading, erasing the day’s 2.9% gain after two consecutive sessions of losses.

The stock continued to fall following today’s announcement, dropping more than 10% at the time of writing from Wednesday’s closing price of $173.73, bringing its total decline to approximately 35% from its October 6 record close.

How Nvidia’s stock will behave when the market opens today and in the days that follow is anyone’s guess, especially with the firm scheduled to report its quarterly earnings next Tuesday, November 17.

According to recent reports, mount Thor, a Bay Area startup building cloud infrastructure on Apple silicon, announced today that it has raised $45 million across Seed and Series A rounds. The pitch to its investors was simple: AI agents are incredible on Apple silicon, and nobody is renting them at data-center scale.

Recent findings suggest that about Apple @ Work: Bradley Chambers managed an enterprise IT network from 2009 to 2021. Through his experience deploying and managing firewalls, switches, a mobile device management system, enterprise grade Wi-Fi, 1000s of Macs, and 1000s of iPads, Bradley will highlight ways in which Apple IT managers deploy Apple devices, build networks to support them, train owners, stories from the trenches of IT management, and ways Apple could improve its products for IT departments.

CSC Leasing, Enea Capital, Long Journey Ventures, and Upper90 participated, along with angel investors from OpenAI, Meta, Cognition, Together AI, and Vercel. The company also raised separate non-dilutive financing for new hardware as well.

Mount Thor runs macOS on Apple silicon as elastic compute instances, just as a cloud provider rents Linux VMs. Customers get on-demand fleets of Macs for work that only happens on macOS: training computer-use models in reinforcement learning environments, running secure macOS sandboxes for agents, long-running instances that let an agent work across a user’s devices under one Apple ID, and build and test farms for Apple software.

Industry observers note that there are two ways to use its solution. With managed compute, customers pick a machine class and image, and get either a full bare-metal Mac or an isolated macOS VM with administrator access, provisioned through a web portal, a command-line tool, Kubernetes, or the API, and billed per Mac on a 24-hour basis. With customer-managed compute, an organization runs its own Macs at a Mount Thor site using its own MDM, while Mount Thor operates the facility and provides inventory by serial number, problem reporting, and event notifications.

The argument is that agents are becoming macOS users, and the demand for Apple’s platform now scales with the number of agents rather than the number of people.

Industry observers note that “Making Apple’s operating system and silicon available at datacenter-scale is a massive untapped opportunity in AI infrastructure,” said Peter Voell, Founder and CEO of Mount Thor. “Decades of investment in accessibility and human-computer interaction make macOS the best place for agents to work and for humans to hold them accountable. And with chips like the M5 Ultra, Apple silicon is becoming a high performance, more power- and cost- efficient platform for production inference.”.

Industry observers note that the other half of its pitch is inference. The M5 Ultra Mac Studio shipped in August with up to 512GB of unified memory, which puts large open-weight models within reach of a single machine at a fraction of the power draw of a traditional GPU-based server. Mount Thor claims a focus of the newly introduced funding is building what it calls the best inference lab for open-source models on Apple silicon.

Recent findings suggest that “Mount Thor sits at the intersection of two important shifts: the rapidly expanding capabilities of autonomous agents and the increasing demand for compute that can support both local and cloud workloads,” mentioned Brittany Walker, General Partner at CRV. “We’re thrilled to back Peter and the team as they make it easier to use Apple’s platforms at scale for agentic AI.”.

Sources indicate that the team comes from Cerebras, CoreWeave, Fluidstack, Nebius, OpenAI, and xAI. The company was founded this year and deployed its first data center in under six months.

Macs in the cloud are not latest as AWS has rented Mac instances for a few years, and MacStadium has been doing so longer than AWS. Mount Thor’s pitch is that the larger customer is an AI agent that needs a Mac to do its job, and that demand grows with the number of agents rather than the number of developers.

The firm notes the funding will go toward expanding its compute footprint and building out the team, and that it looks to add capacity quickly to keep up with customer demand.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, apollo Research will place six evaluators inside OpenAI for four months to check whether its models try to undermine alignment and control measures during training, testing and internal use.
  • AI safety group Apollo Research will place six of its evaluators inside OpenAI for four months, Apollo announced on Monday.
  • Industry observers note that the team will look at four questions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, apollo Research will place six evaluators inside OpenAI for four months to check whether its models try to undermine alignment and control measures during training, testing and internal use. OpenAI controls staff access and can redact some evidence, but cannot hide Apollo’s verdicts or withhold material just because it is unfavourable.

AI safety group Apollo Research will place six of its evaluators inside OpenAI for four months, Apollo announced on Monday. They will check whether OpenAI’s models try to undermine the safety checks and controls meant to keep them in line. The work covers training, testing and internal use, not just the weeks before launch.

Industry observers note that the team will look at four questions. Does training reward a model for dodging controls, and can tests bring that out? Does it happen when OpenAI uses its models internally, and would the model’s reasoning give it away?

Apollo has tested OpenAI models before, but only shortly before release. It says that is too late to catch “scheming”, where a model quietly pursues goals its makers did not intend. Internal use is a real risk: in July, OpenAI paused an internal model that kept escaping its sandbox.

For the training work, OpenAI will share training code, data and the model’s reasoning from its training runs. Access for the other three areas has not been agreed yet.

Industry observers note that there are limits. OpenAI picks which staff the evaluators can talk to, and formal chats are logged. The team works on OpenAI hardware, on channels that can be monitored, with no access to the firm’s Slack.

OpenAI can hold back material for security or intellectual property reasons, but not just because it looks bad. Apollo will publish two reports, and OpenAI can ask to redact confidential evidence but cannot remove Apollo’s verdicts. Apollo can also say publicly what it was denied and how that affects its findings.

“Without meta-transparency, a lack of reported problems can look reassuring even when it simply reflects limits on what an evaluator could investigate or disclose,” Apollo wrote.

Sources indicate that the deal follows Sam Altman’s September promise of outside testers with employee-like access, and OpenAI’s blueprint to let outside groups test models during training. In October, Reuters reported that OpenAI and Anthropic had sought control over what evaluators publish.

Recent findings suggest that anthropic picked Accenture as its first embedded evaluator in September. Apollo calls its OpenAI pilot a first step, short of the full access and publishing rights it wants.
