💡 Key Takeaways
  • Running a small business means wearing a lot of hats.
  • Recent findings suggest that that's where Claude Code comes in.
  • Here are seven practical ways to get started, even if you've never written a line of code.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Running a small business means wearing a lot of hats. One minute you're responding to customers, the next you're updating your website, chasing invoices or trying to figure out why your appointment system isn't working. Hiring someone to handle every task isn't always realistic and be very expensive, especially when you're just starting out.

Recent findings suggest that that's where Claude Code comes in. Anthropic's AI coding assistant can build websites, create custom tools and automate repetitive tasks using everyday language. You describe what you need, and Claude handles much of the technical work, including writing the code.

Here are seven practical ways to get started, even if you've never written a line of code.

Every small business needs an online presence, but creating a website can be expensive and frustrating when you don't know where to start.

Claude Code can generate a website from a description of your business, including pages for your services, prices, contact information and customer testimonials. It can create the website files and help you make changes as you go. You'll still need hosting, a domain name and some testing before making the site public, but you won't necessarily need to write the code yourself.

For example, a local bakery could ask Claude to create a mobile-friendly website with a menu, photo gallery and custom cake inquiry form.

Try this prompt: Build a modern, mobile-friendly website for my small bakery. Include a homepage, menu, about page, photo gallery and contact form. Use a warm, welcoming design with simple navigation. Explain how I can preview the website and what I need to do before publishing it.

If you run a salon, are a personal trainer, tutor or run a cleaning service, managing appointments through emails and text messages can rapidly become overwhelming.

Claude Code can help you build a booking interface that lets customers request appointments, select services and provide contact information.

You could also ask it to help connect the interface to an existing scheduling platform, although that requires compatible integrations and proper authentication. As you probably know all too well, the goal is to spend less time coordinating schedules and more time helping customers. Just make sure the finished system prevents double bookings and protects customer information before you rely on it.

Sources indicate that try this prompt: Create a simple appointment-booking website for my tutoring business. Customers should be able to choose a subject, select an available time and enter their contact information. Include an administrator view where I can manage appointment requests. Explain what additional services are needed to make real bookings work.

This might be one of the most useful applications for service businesses because it involves pricing questions that you get time and time again.

Now, instead of answering the same pricing questions repeatedly, you could offer an online calculator that gives customers a preliminary estimate based on their home's size and the services they need.

Claude Code can build the interface and calculations around your own pricing rules. This one take a little extra time up front because you would need to supply accurate prices and test the calculations, but the result could make it easier for potential customers to understand your services without contacting you first.

Try this prompt: Build an interactive pricing calculator for lawn care business. Customers should enter their yard's square footage, indicate any flower beds, swimming pools or other extras such as swing sets, and whether they want front, back or both. Create an estimated price using rules I can easily edit. Display the total instantly and add a button to request a final quote.

Keeping up with customers is important, but writing individual follow-up messages can take time away from running your business. Claude Code can help create a system that organizes customer information and drafts personalized follow-up emails.

Try this prompt: Create a simple customer follow-up tool for my landscaping business. I want to upload a CSV file containing customer names, email addresses and their last appointment dates. Identify customers who haven't booked a service in six months and draft a friendly, personalized reminder for each person. Let me review everything before sending.

Industry observers note that creating invoices is simple enough when you have a handful of customers. Once your business grows, tracking what's been sent, paid or forgotten becomes another job.

Claude Code can build a lightweight invoicing tool that creates downloadable invoices, organizes payment records and identifies outstanding balances.

A freelance photographer, for example, could create an invoice generator that calculates package prices, adds optional services and produces a professional PDF. You can later explore connecting the system to an existing accounting platform, although financial integrations require additional setup.

For anything involving taxes, financial reporting or payment processing, verify the results and use established financial services where appropriate.

Try this prompt: Build an invoice generator for my photography business. Let me enter customer details, services, prices, taxes and payment due dates. Generate a professional PDF invoice with my business information. Include a dashboard where I can manually mark invoices as paid or unpaid.

According to recent reports, whether you sell handmade jewelry, run a small boutique or manage supplies for a cleaning tech giant, inventory can be surprisingly difficult to track. Claude Code can create a custom dashboard that organizes products, tracks stock levels and flags items that need to be reordered. This could be a great idea if you're still tracking inventory manually in spreadsheets.You can tailor the tool to your specific business. For businesses selling through multiple channels, you'll still need reliable synchronization with your sales systems to keep stock counts accurate.

According to recent reports, try this prompt: Create a simple inventory management dashboard for my handmade candle business. I need to track product names, quantities, costs and selling prices. Highlight products when inventory falls below five units. Add the ability to import and export inventory using CSV files.

Running a business means making decisions based on numbers, but those numbers are often scattered across spreadsheets, sales reports and other files.

Claude Code can help you combine the information into a simple dashboard showing sales, expenses, popular products and other key metrics.

For example, a coffee shop owner could upload sales data and generate charts showing their busiest days, best-selling drinks and average daily revenue. You could start with a dashboard that runs on your own computer and expand it later if your needs change. The notable part is making sure Claude interprets the data correctly.

Try this prompt: Build a small business dashboard that lets me upload CSV files containing daily sales. Show total revenue, average order value, best-selling products and sales trends over time. Include charts that are easy to understand and a way to filter results by date. Keep the data stored locally for the initial version.

Get started by going to Claude Code's website and choosing a supported way to access it. Depending on your device and preferred workflow, you can use its desktop application, terminal interface or web experience.

According to recent reports, claude Code is included with Claude Pro, which costs $20 per month when billed monthly, although usage limits apply. Other plans and API-based billing options are also available.

According to recent reports, once you're set up, choose one small problem rather than trying to build an entire business management system. Describe what you want the tool to accomplish, who will use it and what information it needs. Ask Claude to create a simple prototype first, explain how to run it and help you test it.

You can then make changes by describing what's wrong or what you'd like to improve. Of course, before connecting customer records, payment information or other sensitive business data, review the tool's permissions and security. AI-generated code can contain mistakes, and anything customers depend on needs thorough testing.

Sources indicate that claude Code won't replace every service your business needs, and using it doesn't eliminate the responsibility of maintaining the tools you build. But it does make custom software more accessible to people who previously had to hire a developer or settle for whatever features their existing apps offered.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cleaning windows is one of my favorite quick tasks because it takes so little time. But even after wiping the glass spotless using my go-to white vinegar and dish soap solution and dusting the windowsills, there is always one specific spot I often overlook in my regular cleaning routine.

Industry observers note that in fact, it’s the one place that nobody bothers to look at — dusty window tracks. These usually contain all sorts of grime, from dust and debris buildup to dead bugs; they are also notoriously tricky to clean properly. Even a narrow vacuum attachment isn't enough to get deep into window tracks and reach those awkward corners.

Industry observers note that that was until I found this clever hack that simply involves a popular pantry staple that you’ll probably have in your kitchen. What’s more, professional cleaners swear by this quick cleaning trick — that only takes minutes. Here’s why and how you use it.

According to recent reports, baking soda is a versatile powerhouse for tackling everyday home challenges — from breaking down stubborn stains to neutralizing unpleasant odors. Beyond these common uses, though, it also proves to be effective at deep cleaning window tracks.

This is because baking soda acts as a mild abrasive that can lift grime with ease (scratch-free), and when combined with white vinegar (my go-to), it can easily create a great cleaning solution with its natural properties.

According to recent reports, if you want to know more, check out what makes baking soda and white vinegar so good at cleaning. Just avoid these 7 things you should never clean with baking soda.

It has been revealed that start by clearing out any loose debris or dust, using a narrow nozzle attachment on a powerful vacuum cleaner. Next, sprinkle a layer of baking soda along the dirty window track before spraying with white vinegar.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Leave to sit for about five minutes to allow the fizzing chemical reaction to get to work on the ingrained dirt and dust. If the track is especially grimy, leave it for up to 15 minutes.

Then grab an old toothbrush or small bristle brush to gently scrub away the grime from top to bottom — not forgetting to tackle the corners and awkward crevices. You’ll see the dirt will easily lift off, making the task quick and hassle-free.

After removing dirt and debris from the tracks, wipe away any remaining baking soda and vinegar with a paper towel or microfiber cloth. Then finish the job by cracking open the window so the track can air-dry completely.

So if you want to keep your windows looking spotless all year round, be sure to include this simple 5-minute trick in your regular cleaning routine.

Donald Trump boards Air Force One at Salina Regional Airport in Salina, Kansas, 1 November 2026.

It has been revealed that the bosses of some of China’s biggest technology companies are on the agenda of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit in Shenzhen, which starts on Tuesday. The organiser released the agenda on Monday, Bloomberg and Reuters reported.

According to recent reports, robin Zeng, founder and chairman of battery maker CATL, and Baidu chairman and CEO Robin Li are among the speakers. Wang Xingxing, founder of humanoid robot maker Unitree, will also speak. BYD chairman Wang Chuanfu and Xiaomi CEO Lei Jun are due on panels, and the chairmen of ICBC, Bank of China and Agricultural Bank of China will attend, Reuters reported.

Recent findings suggest that the US names include the CEOs of Visa, Mastercard and UPS, Boeing global president Brendan Nelson and Google’s head of government affairs, Karan Bhatia. PwC global chairman Mohamed Kande and Deloitte CEO Joe Ucuzoglu are also on the list, according to Reuters.

Xi Jinping will open the two-day summit at the Qianhai International Convention Center with a keynote speech. The organiser, the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade (CCPIT), declared it in a statement. Leaders of 11 other economies, including Russia, Canada and South Korea, will give speeches or join panels.

In a recent development, more than 2,000 political and business leaders are expected, from 115 Fortune Global 500 companies among others. US companies make up nearly 20% of the foreign participants, the largest group from outside China, the council said. More than 130 Shenzhen companies are taking part.

Industry observers note that chinese business leaders stayed away from Xi’s state visit to Washington in September, Bloomberg reported. Ahead of the summit, Shenzhen suspended drone deliveries and reduced robotaxi services, the Associated Press reported.

It has been revealed that elon Musk, the head of Tesla and SpaceX, will travel with President Donald Trump to Shenzhen. Senior US officials said so on a call with reporters on Friday, CNBC reported. One official said Musk could act as an adviser to the president.

“Obviously, he has tremendous business interests in the U.S.-China relationship,” the official said.

Musk will not join the three-way meeting of Trump, Xi and Russia’s Vladimir Putin, officials told the Associated Press. On the same call, officials noted Trump did not blueprint to raise the Nvidia spy allegations with Xi.

“In all of our discussions and negotiations with the Chinese, we do not negotiate American export controls,” an official mentioned.

Sources indicate that on Monday, the Commerce Department issued a rule to stop Chinese companies renting AI chips remotely through overseas data centres. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is joining the trip.

According to recent reports, CATL, Baidu and Unitree are on the US Department of Defense’s Section 1260H list of “Chinese military companies”. Beijing has criticised the list. In July, Washington also tightened curbs on some foreign-made robots, citing possible supply chain vulnerabilities, Bloomberg reported.

The CEO summit runs on 17 and 18 November. The APEC leaders’ meeting follows on 18 and 19 November, where Trump is due to meet Xi.

In a recent development, senior officials meeting in Shenzhen over the weekend prepared work on trade, connectivity and AI for the leaders, the APEC Secretariat stated. It includes China’s proposed statement on the digital economy and AI, which calls for wider use of the technology in health care, education and energy and for safe and trusted AI development.

Recent findings suggest that the Halliday G2 AI smart glasses are a step in the right direction, delivering camera-less specs with helpful AI features in a comfortable yet chunky (and dorky) design. But these smart glasses offer a near-identical experience to their rivals, all while not quite hitting the mark. Clear, bright waveguide display.

It has been revealed that why you can trust Tom's Guide Our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you. Find out more about how we test, analyze, and rate.

When I first heard of Halliday making a splash back at CES 2025 by putting an "invisible" built-in display into its smart glasses, I was amazed by what the future of smart specs holds. Now, the company has refined its AI smart glasses in the Halliday G2, but this time, it isn't quite as revolutionary.

In a recent development, with its dual micro LED engines and waveguide optics on both lenses to deliver a simplistic green dot matrix style text, an open-ear audio system for personal sound and a bundle of features utilizing a Halliday AI assistant, the Halliday G2 AI smart glasses are a subtle pair of specs made for seamless daily wear. Well, I say "subtle" loosely, as everyone will know that you're wearing smart glasses with these on. And wait, many of these features sound a little too familiar...

These aren't just taking cues from the Even Realities G2, as the Halliday G2 offers like-for-like features in the exact same waveguide display format. I mean, it's even called "G2," for pete's sake! From the Meeting Flow feature that can summarize, research and transcribe conversations in meetings, which is just the Even Realities G2's Conversate feature, to the Cheat Sheet feature that acts as a teleprompter, which is just Teleprompt on the Even Realities G2, there's not a lot here to pick these over its clear inspiration.

But that's not to say its features aren't handy to use, especially when it comes to its Halliday AI, which is snappy at answering whatever you ask. Along with its informative dashboard (such as displaying the time, weather and more), notifications that are clear to read and its helpful Translate feature, there are day-to-day benefits of wearing the Halliday G2s. That said, it's still held back by other annoyances, like a subpar open-ear audio system and a Stealth Mode that doesn't do a good job at being "stealthy.".

But are these the best smart glasses for you? After wearing the Halliday G2 daily, here are my thoughts.

Dual micro-LED, 600 x 300 per-eye resolution, 1,600 nits peak brightness.

The Halliday G2s have clearly come a long way from their first iteration, making for a commendable pair of AI smart glasses that focus on everyday wear with helpful features, rather than "pervy glasses" with a camera in them.

Recent findings suggest that when first seeing the Halliday G2, I made an all-too-quick assumption that these would give my head and ears a tough time. These are thick, blocky specs, and I could almost see how much they weigh from the look of them. But I was wrong.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

In a recent development, coming in at just 1.7 ounces, the Hallifay G2s are actually one of the more comfortable AI glasses I've worn. The magnesium alloy frame keeps the weight off, but the glasses themselves have a good distribution of weight with the tech that is housed in their temples.

Not quite as light or slim as the Even Realities G2 (1.2 ounces), but around a similar size and weight to the Ray-Ban Meta (Gen 2) at around 1.79 ounces.

While I wouldn't say these feel premium to the touch, especially for the price, I would have these smart specs sitting on my face all day without being irritated by sore ears or frame imprints on my nose or around my eyes.

Most of its tech, from the 210 mAh battery to the open-ear audio it boasts, is housed in the thick temples (also like the Ray-Ban Meta specs). This makes them naturally thick, but this works out, as it makes gesture control along the right temple easier to manage. That includes tapping and swiping to navigate around in-display menus and features.

It takes a little while to get the hang of, but it works like a charm once it clicks, and the bar-like temples make it easy to swipe and slide a finger along.

You'll also find a Halliday G2 hard case, and it's sturdy, stylish and sizeable enough to easily slip in the G2s and close its strong magnetic clasp. It's no Even Realities G2 smart case that charges the glasses, but it does a fine job of keeping the Halliday G2s protected.

It has been revealed that this is one of the first signs of similarities between the Halliday G2 and Even Realities G2. But this is a nice trait to share, because it's wonderful to have a discreet display that blends into the real world as an overlay that's easy to see and read.

Using dual micro-LED engines to cover both lenses, the Halliday G2s feature binocular waveguide displays for a minimal, yet extremely helpful, dashboard right in front of your eyes.

Sources indicate that as with the Even Realities G2, the display is made up of green dot-matrix-style text, akin to the Pip-Boy from "Fallout." It's not obtrusive, and it makes it easy to glance at while going about your day. It helps that the waveguides have a 600 x 300 per-eye resolution and a whopping 1,600 nits of peak brightness. And yes, that means I could clearly see the display even during bright days (those are now limited in the U.K.).

Sources indicate that whether it's notifications coming in via your smartphone or the dashboard displaying the weather forecast for the next few hours, text is clear, bright and sharp, yet doesn't overtake your full real-world view, either. This is the kind of simplistic, futuristic display I've come to enjoy in smart glasses, so keep on this path, Halliday!

Having a personal HUD to show you the time, date, weather forecast and more at a glance is already a nice perk, but using the Halliday G2 to summarize conversations, translate languages in real time, give you instant answers just by asking it and view text via a teleprompter is what makes these glasses actually "smart.".

The Halliday G2's key features include Meeting Flow, where live AI agents manage whole conversations (geared towards business meetings) by tracking, summarizing, transcribing and quickly researching what is noted; Cheatsheet, a teleprompter that's (sort of) invisible to everyone but you, with customizable read speeds; and Translation, which can translate conversations in real time for over 45 different languages.

Meeting Flow is the star of the show, and it did a great job of getting all the key points noted in one of my daily stand-up meetings and organizing this into different sections, such as having a To-Do List and a Quick Summary of everything that was said. I also quite liked the Thread Tracker, which helps you get back on topic before the conversation goes off the rails (which is a fun problem I generally have in meetings).

Recent findings suggest that now, there are plenty of AI agents that do this automatically in virtual meetings, like Google Gemini, Otter AI and plenty more. But the Halliday G2s give you a personal meeting assistant right in your view during meetings, which can be helpful to many.

In a recent development, cheatsheet and Translate are also snappy in action, and I was impressed with the Halliday AI assistant being able to answer random questions on the fly. For example, while I was watching the cult classic "Twin Peaks," I asked where it was generally filmed, and it was quick to answer (it's in Snoqualmie Valley near Seattle).

It has been revealed that do any of these features sound familiar? They should, as you'll find all these Halliday G2 features on the Even Realities G2 — just named differently. For example, Conversate on the Even Realities is just Meeting Flow here, while Teleprompt is Cheat Sheet and Translate is... Translate.

While these features are like-for-like, that doesn't make Halliday's tools any less helpful, as they still do what they set out to do well.

Unless you're looking for thick, Spongebob-like glasses, the Halliday G2s aren't the most seamless smart glasses you can get, and they have far too much in common with the Even Realities G2, but with a couple more downsides, to stand out.

I can almost hear Homer Simpson shouting "Neeerd!" out of his car when I put on the Halliday G2s, and that alone makes me avoid wearing these in public.

The G2s are clearly smart glasses, as everyone I came across had pointed out at first glance. That's not such a terrible thing, but it's just how thick and bulky the smart specs are that makes them unappealing. Of course, glasses come in all shapes and sizes, and some frame styles are better suited to others. Some may enjoy the bulkiness, but there is a limit to frames being too thick, too.

Along with this, it's a shame there is only one style of the Halliday G2s, unlike the many different frames of the Ray-Ban Meta lineup and the couple of options the Even Realities G2 offers.

While the waveguide displays are discreet, others can still see the green light from the lenses at certain angles. That's why the Halliday G2 smart glasses have a Stealth Mode, so you can subtly read incoming messages or AI conversations without that green hue people may be able to see.

Or, that's what it wants to do anyway. In reality, it simply dims the green text on the waveguide displays, but it's still able to be seen at different angles (as my friends have confirmed). It's not as noticeable when Stealth Mode is turned off, but I wouldn't exactly call this stealthy.

At the very least, Stealth Mode on the Halliday G2s aren't as creepy as smart glasses with cameras, seeing as it's just text.

The only major difference between the Halliday G2 and Even Realities G2 is that the former comes with an open-ear audio system, much like the Ray-Ban Meta glasses. You can hear phone calls, listen to music or podcasts and hear a very annoying clicking sound with each action you do.

Sources indicate that I'd prefer to not have any audio in smart glasses aimed at being everyday specs for the usual glasses wearer, especially when sound easily leaks out for everyone to hear what you're listening to, and it sounds more hollow than anything else. I also imagine the G2's battery takes a hit from this, being just around 12 hours before needing a charge. Not bad, but the Even Realities G2 can last a couple of days before needing a boost.

I understand that it's trying to be the all-in-one system for your face, so you no longer need one of the best earbuds, but it's far from accomplishing that task. And yes, I turned off that navigation click as soon as I heard it, which also meant turning off the ringtone.

Industry observers note that the Halliday G2 are the type of AI smart glasses that I'm a fan of, offering a comfortable fit for all-day wear with helpful AI features that are intuitive to use and snappy in action. Being able to check the time or weather on the fly without having to take out your phone, summarize conversations with key talking points and translate other languages are huge perks to have sitting on your face.

But the Halliday G2s succumb to the usual problem with smart glasses: they look too "smart." That's fine if major, chunky frames suit your style, but when the Even Realities G2 does it all better at the same retail price, but in a more casual design, then it's harder to recommend these over its competition.

While the Halliday G2 AI smart glasses are a step in the right direction, there are still a few features and design choices that the best smart glasses we recommend do better.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that iOS 27 is packed with new features, including several for the Find My app.
  • Apple’s Find My app is a great way to share your location with friends or family members on either permanent or a temporary basis.
  • But the “temporary” option just got a very welcome upgrade in iOS 27.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that iOS 27 is packed with new features, including several for the Find My app. One upgrade to Find My—custom sharing durations—grants a feature request I’ve had for years.

Apple’s Find My app is a great way to share your location with friends or family members on either permanent or a temporary basis.

But the “temporary” option just got a very welcome upgrade in iOS 27.

That’s because you can now set up location sharing in Find My for a custom duration. Per Apple:.

Recent findings suggest that consumers [now] have more control over how they share their location with friends and family using Find My, with fresh options to share for a custom duration — either for a number of minutes, hours, or days — or even set a date and time for when sharing will stop. This makes it easy for users to share their location while attending an event, or for a long weekend getaway with friends and family.

Until iOS 27, you could only choose from a very limited set of “temporary” options for sharing: for one hour, or until end of day. The only other option was “indefinitely.”.

The main time I find myself adding new people to share my location with, I’m either traveling or they’re visiting me. On these occasions, the “one hour” and “until end of day” options never cut it.

So of course, I have to choose “indefinitely.” Then there’s the decision after the trip ends of either continuing to let location sharing happen, or ending sharing immediately (if I remember to). And the latter option has always felt a little awkward to me. I’d much rather schedule the sharing duration upfront.

In a recent development, and now with iOS 27 I can. When sharing location with someone, a fresh ‘Custom’ duration option allows choosing an end date and time, and/or manually setting a given number of days, hours, and minutes for sharing to continue.

It’s a great change, long overdue, and works perfectly for the scenarios Apple outlined.

Sources indicate that have you ever wished for custom sharing durations in Find My? Let us know in the comments.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Opera today revealed that its Data Saver feature is now available on iOS, in a press release that also revealed a 20% year-over-year increase in the browser’s monthly active users.
  • In a press release published today, Opera celebrated a 20% year-over-year increase in monthly active users on iOS last month, “building on its established presence in Asia and Africa while expanding its reach in the US and Europe.”.
  • In the US alone, growth was even stronger, with monthly active people increasing 46% year over year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Opera today revealed that its Data Saver feature is now available on iOS, in a press release that also revealed a 20% year-over-year increase in the browser’s monthly active users. Here are the details.

In a press release published today, Opera celebrated a 20% year-over-year increase in monthly active users on iOS last month, “building on its established presence in Asia and Africa while expanding its reach in the US and Europe.”.

In the US alone, growth was even stronger, with monthly active people increasing 46% year over year.

In both cases, that outpaced the 16% year-over-year growth Opera reported on PC just a few days ago, when the manufacturer also announced it had surpassed 100 million monthly active consumers for the first time.

Behind this growth across both desktop and mobile is a broader shift in consumer expectations – customers are increasingly reconsidering the default as their understanding of what a browser can do evolves.

In today’s announcement, Opera also touted the arrival of Data Saver on Opera One for iOS, which the manufacturer claims can reduce browsing data usage by up to 80% by compressing images and text on its servers before they reach the user’s device.

For users, this can make a difference when travelling abroad on expensive roaming data, topping up a prepaid proposal or running low on a monthly data bundle. Data Saver can also help when browsing on a weak connection.

While the press release didn’t go into detail on the privacy aspects of the feature, it did note that “the feature is optional, and consumers can switch it on or off and see how much data they have saved.”.

Apple HomeView introduces tomorrow, but its first security update is already here

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • While the first HomeView units won’t reach customers until tomorrow, Apple today released a software upgrade addressing nine security vulnerabilities.
  • Apple today released HomeView Software Version 27.2 (build 24V526), which contains some of the security fixes the company included in recent updates to its other operating systems, including iOS 27.2, macOS 27.2 Golden Gate, and iPadOS 27.2.
  • These include a vulnerability that could allow a remote attacker to join an iMessage group chat and receive its messages, as well as another that could allow a malicious Bluetooth device to pair without user interaction.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

While the first HomeView units won’t reach customers until tomorrow, Apple today released a software upgrade addressing nine security vulnerabilities. Here are the details.

Apple today released HomeView Software Version 27.2 (build 24V526), which contains some of the security fixes the company included in recent updates to its other operating systems, including iOS 27.2, macOS 27.2 Golden Gate, and iPadOS 27.2.

These include a vulnerability that could allow a remote attacker to join an iMessage group chat and receive its messages, as well as another that could allow a malicious Bluetooth device to pair without user interaction.

In practice, this means that people who get the device starting tomorrow are advised to enhancement it as soon as possible, since the vulnerabilities have been publicly disclosed.

Here’s the full security content of HomeView Software Version 27.2.

Impact: An attacker in Bluetooth range may be able to bypass the rate limit on pairing code attempts.

Description: A logic matter was addressed with improved state management.

Impact: An app may be able to access sensitive user data.

Description: An authorization issue was addressed with improved state management.

Impact: An attacker in Bluetooth range may be able to corrupt process memory.

Description: A use-after-free concern was addressed with improved memory management.

Impact: Processing maliciously crafted input may lead to memory corruption.

Description: An out-of-bounds write glitch was addressed with improved input validation.

Impact: A malicious Bluetooth device may be able to establish a pairing without user interaction.

Description: This concern was addressed with improved checks.

Impact: An attacker in Bluetooth range may be able to bypass the rate limit on pairing code attempts and pair with a device without user interaction.

Description: A logic issue was addressed with improved state management.

CVE-2026-113964: an anonymous researcher.

Impact: A remote attacker may be able to join an iMessage group chat and receive its messages.

Description: An authorization issue was addressed with improved validation.

CVE-2026-113961: an anonymous researcher.

Impact: A user added to an iMessage group may be able to access messages sent before they joined.

Description: This issue was addressed by removing the vulnerable code.

CVE-2026-113960: an anonymous researcher.

Impact: An attacker on the same network may be able to bypass the rate limit on AirPlay pairing code attempts.

Description: A logic issue was addressed with improved state management.

Earlier today, Apple also confirmed that a software enhancement coming next month will add support for security accessories to HomeView’s Siri AI, which currently refuses to unlock doors or open garage doors via voice commands.

Be sure to catch 9to5Mac’s full review of Apple HomeView ahead of tomorrow’s launch.

#3993. Industry News: Andrew Ng: Unbiggen AI

📅 09 Feb 2022 • ⏱️ 14m • 📚 Deep Dive (2890 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ieee ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: Andrew Ng: Unbiggen AI

📅 09 Feb 2022 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2890 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ieee

⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The AI pioneer states it’s time for smart-sized, “data-centric” solutions to big problems.
  • Andrew Ng was involved in the rise of massive deep learning models trained on vast amounts of data, but now he’s preaching small-data solutions.
  • Recent findings suggest that andrew Ng has serious street cred in artificial intelligence.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The AI pioneer states it’s time for smart-sized, “data-centric” solutions to big problems.

Andrew Ng was involved in the rise of massive deep learning models trained on vast amounts of data, but now he’s preaching small-data solutions.

Recent findings suggest that andrew Ng has serious street cred in artificial intelligence. He pioneered the use of graphics processing units (GPUs) to train deep learning models in the late 2000s with his students at Stanford University, cofounded Google Brain in 2011, and then served for three years as chief scientist for Baidu, where he helped build the Chinese tech giant’s AI group. So when he says he has identified the next significant shift in artificial intelligence, people listen. And that’s what he told IEEE Spectrum in an exclusive Q&A.

Recent findings suggest that ng’s current efforts are focused on his company Landing AI, which built a platform called LandingLens to help manufacturers improve visual inspection with computer vision. He has also become something of an evangelist for what he calls the data-centric AI movement, which he says can yield “small data” solutions to major issues in AI, including model efficiency, accuracy, and bias.

Recent findings suggest that the great advances in deep learning over the past decade or so have been powered by ever-bigger models crunching ever-bigger amounts of data. Some people argue that that’s an unsustainable trajectory. Do you agree that it can’t go on that way?

Andrew Ng: This is a massive question. We’ve seen foundation models in NLP [natural language processing]. I’m excited about NLP models getting even bigger, and also about the potential of building foundation models in computer vision. I think there’s lots of signal to still be exploited in video: We have not been able to build foundation models yet for video because of compute bandwidth and the cost of processing video, as opposed to tokenized text. So I think that this engine of scaling up deep learning algorithms, which has been running for something like 15 years now, still has steam in it. Having said that, it only applies to certain problems, and there’s a set of other problems that need small data solutions.

When you say you want a foundation model for computer vision, what do you mean by that?

Sources indicate that ng: This is a term coined by Percy Liang and some of my friends at Stanford to refer to very large models, trained on very large data sets, that can be tuned for specific applications. For example, GPT-3 is an example of a foundation model [for NLP]. Foundation models offer a lot of promise as a fresh paradigm in developing machine learning applications, but also challenges in terms of making sure that they’re reasonably fair and free from bias, especially if many of us will be building on top of them.

What needs to happen for someone to build a foundation model for video?

Industry observers note that ng: I think there is a scalability problem. The compute power needed to process the large volume of images for video is significant, and I think that’s why foundation models have arisen first in NLP. Many researchers are working on this, and I think we’re seeing early signs of such models being developed in computer vision. But I’m confident that if a semiconductor maker gave us 10 times more processor power, we could easily find 10 times more video to build such models for vision.

Having said that, a lot of what’s happened over the past decade is that deep learning has happened in consumer-facing companies that have large user bases, sometimes billions of consumers, and therefore very large data sets. While that paradigm of machine learning has driven a lot of economic value in consumer software, I find that that recipe of scale doesn’t work for other industries.

It’s funny to hear you say that, because your early work was at a consumer-facing company with millions of users.

Industry observers note that ng: Over a decade ago, when I proposed starting the Google Brain project to use Google’s compute infrastructure to build very large neural networks, it was a controversial step. One very senior person pulled me aside and warned me that starting Google Brain would be bad for my career. I think he felt that the action couldn’t just be in scaling up, and that I should instead focus on architecture innovation.

“In many industries where giant data sets simply don’t exist, I think the focus has to shift from big data to good data. Having 50 thoughtfully engineered examples can be sufficient to explain to the neural network what you want it to learn.” —Andrew Ng, CEO & Founder, Landing AI.

According to recent reports, I remember when my students and I published the first NeurIPS workshop paper advocating using CUDA, a platform for processing on GPUs, for deep learning—a different senior person in AI sat me down and stated, “CUDA is really complicated to program. As a programming paradigm, this seems like too much work.” I did manage to convince him; the other person I did not convince.

I expect they’re both convinced now.

Over the past year as I’ve been speaking to people about the data-centric AI movement, I’ve been getting flashbacks to when I was speaking to people about deep learning and scalability 10 or 15 years ago. In the past year, I’ve been getting the same mix of “there’s nothing fresh here” and “this seems like the wrong direction.”.

How do you define data-centric AI, and why do you consider it a movement?

It has been revealed that ng: Data-centric AI is the discipline of systematically engineering the data needed to successfully build an AI system. For an AI system, you have to implement some algorithm, say a neural network, in code and then train it on your data set. The dominant paradigm over the last decade was to download the data set while you focus on improving the code. Thanks to that paradigm, over the last decade deep learning networks have improved significantly, to the point where for a lot of applications the code—the neural network architecture—is basically a solved problem. So for many practical applications, it’s now more productive to hold the neural network architecture fixed, and instead find ways to improve the data.

When I started speaking about this, there were many practitioners who, completely appropriately, raised their hands and said, “Yes, we’ve been doing this for 20 years.” This is the time to take the things that some individuals have been doing intuitively and make it a systematic engineering discipline.

According to recent reports, the data-centric AI movement is much bigger than one organization or group of researchers. My collaborators and I organized a data-centric AI workshop at NeurIPS, and I was really delighted at the number of authors and presenters that highlighted up.

You often talk about companies or institutions that have only a small amount of data to work with. How can data-centric AI help them?

Ng: You hear a lot about vision systems built with millions of images—I once built a face recognition system using 350 million images. Architectures built for hundreds of millions of images don’t work with only 50 images. But it turns out, if you have 50 really good examples, you can build something valuable, like a defect-inspection system. In many industries where giant data sets simply don’t exist, I think the focus has to shift from substantial data to good data. Having 50 thoughtfully engineered examples can be sufficient to explain to the neural network what you want it to learn.

When you talk about training a model with just 50 images, does that really mean you’re taking an existing model that was trained on a very large data set and fine-tuning it? Or do you mean a brand fresh model that’s designed to learn only from that small data set?

Ng: Let me describe what Landing AI does. When doing visual inspection for manufacturers, we often use our own flavor of RetinaNet. It is a pretrained model. Having said that, the pretraining is a small piece of the puzzle. What’s a bigger piece of the puzzle is providing tools that enable the manufacturer to pick the right set of images [to use for fine-tuning] and label them in a consistent way. There’s a very practical problem we’ve seen spanning vision, NLP, and speech, where even human annotators don’t agree on the appropriate label. For significant data applications, the common response has been: If the data is noisy, let’s just get a lot of data and the algorithm will average over it. But if you can develop tools that flag where the data’s inconsistent and give you a very targeted way to improve the consistency of the data, that turns out to be a more efficient way to get a high-performing system.

“Collecting more data often helps, but if you try to collect more data for everything, that can be a very expensive activity.” —Andrew Ng.

Industry observers note that for example, if you have 10,000 images where 30 images are of one class, and those 30 images are labeled inconsistently, one of the things we do is build tools to draw your attention to the subset of data that’s inconsistent. So you can very rapidly relabel those images to be more consistent, and this leads to improvement in performance.

Could this focus on high-quality data help with bias in data sets? If you’re able to curate the data more before training?

According to recent reports, ng: Very much so. Many researchers have pointed out that biased data is one factor among many leading to biased systems. There have been many thoughtful efforts to engineer the data. At the NeurIPS workshop, Olga Russakovsky gave a really nice talk on this. At the main NeurIPS conference, I also really enjoyed Mary Gray’s presentation, which touched on how data-centric AI is one piece of the solution, but not the entire solution. Latest tools like Datasheets for Datasets also seem like an important piece of the puzzle.

Industry observers note that one of the powerful tools that data-centric AI gives us is the ability to engineer a subset of the data. Imagine training a machine-learning system and finding that its performance is okay for most of the data set, but its performance is biased for just a subset of the data. If you try to change the whole neural network architecture to improve the performance on just that subset, it’s quite difficult. But if you can engineer a subset of the data you can address the problem in a much more targeted way.

When you talk about engineering the data, what do you mean exactly?

Ng: In AI, data cleaning is important, but the way the data has been cleaned has often been in very manual ways. In computer vision, someone may visualize images through a Jupyter notebook and maybe spot the problem, and maybe fix it. But I’m excited about tools that allow you to have a very large data set, tools that draw your attention rapidly and efficiently to the subset of data where, say, the labels are noisy. Or to quickly bring your attention to the one class among 100 classes where it would benefit you to collect more data. Collecting more data often helps, but if you try to collect more data for everything, that can be a very expensive activity.

For example, I once figured out that a speech-recognition system was performing poorly when there was car noise in the background. Knowing that allowed me to collect more data with car noise in the background, rather than trying to collect more data for everything, which would have been expensive and slow.

What about using synthetic data, is that often a good solution?

It has been revealed that ng: I think synthetic data is an key tool in the tool chest of data-centric AI. At the NeurIPS workshop, Anima Anandkumar gave a great talk that touched on synthetic data. I think there are important uses of synthetic data that go beyond just being a preprocessing step for increasing the data set for a learning algorithm. I’d love to see more tools to let developers use synthetic data generation as part of the closed loop of iterative machine learning development.

Do you mean that synthetic data would allow you to try the model on more data sets?

Ng: Not really. Here’s an example. Let’s say you’re trying to detect defects in a smartphone casing. There are many different types of defects on smartphones. It could be a scratch, a dent, pit marks, discoloration of the material, other types of blemishes. If you train the model and then find through error analysis that it’s doing well overall but it’s performing poorly on pit marks, then synthetic data generation allows you to address the problem in a more targeted way. You could generate more data just for the pit-mark category.

“In the consumer software Internet, we could train a handful of machine-learning models to serve a billion owners. In manufacturing, you might have 10,000 manufacturers building 10,000 custom AI models.” —Andrew Ng.

Industry observers note that synthetic data generation is a very powerful tool, but there are many simpler tools that I will often try first. Such as data augmentation, improving labeling consistency, or just asking a factory to collect more data.

Recent findings suggest that to make these issues more concrete, can you walk me through an example? When a tech giant approaches Landing AI and says it has a problem with visual inspection, how do you onboard them and work toward deployment?

Ng: When a customer approaches us we usually have a conversation about their inspection problem and look at a few images to verify that the problem is feasible with computer vision. Assuming it is, we ask them to upload the data to the LandingLens platform. We often advise them on the methodology of data-centric AI and help them label the data.

According to recent reports, one of the foci of Landing AI is to empower manufacturing companies to do the machine learning work themselves. A lot of our work is making sure the software is fast and easy to use. Through the iterative process of machine learning development, we advise customers on things like how to train models on the platform, when and how to improve the labeling of data so the performance of the model improves. Our training and software supports them all the way through deploying the trained model to an edge device in the factory.

How do you deal with changing needs? If products change or lighting conditions change in the factory, can the model keep up?

It has been revealed that ng: It varies by manufacturer. There is data drift in many contexts. But there are some manufacturers that have been running the same manufacturing line for 20 years now with few changes, so they don’t expect changes in the next five years. Those stable environments make things easier. For other manufacturers, we provide tools to flag when there’s a significant data-drift issue. I find it really important to empower manufacturing customers to correct data, retrain, and upgrade the model. Because if something changes and it’s 3 a.m. in the United States, I want them to be able to adapt their learning algorithm right away to maintain operations.

Recent findings suggest that in the consumer software Internet, we could train a handful of machine-learning models to serve a billion users. In manufacturing, you might have 10,000 manufacturers building 10,000 custom AI models. The challenge is, how do you do that without Landing AI having to hire 10,000 machine learning specialists?

So you’re saying that to make it scale, you have to empower customers to do a lot of the training and other work.

Ng: Yes, exactly! This is an industry-wide problem in AI, not just in manufacturing. Look at health care. Every hospital has its own slightly different format for electronic health records. How can every hospital train its own custom AI model? Expecting every hospital’s IT personnel to invent upcoming neural-network architectures is unrealistic. The only way out of this dilemma is to build tools that empower the customers to build their own models by giving them tools to engineer the data and express their domain knowledge. That’s what Landing AI is executing in computer vision, and the field of AI needs other teams to execute this in other domains.

Is there anything else you think it’s vital for people to understand about the work you’re doing or the data-centric AI movement?

Sources indicate that ng: In the last decade, the biggest shift in AI was a shift to deep learning. I think it’s quite possible that in this decade the biggest shift will be to data-centric AI. With the maturity of today’s neural network architectures, I think for a lot of the practical applications the bottleneck will be whether we can efficiently get the data we need to develop systems that work well. The data-centric AI movement has tremendous energy and momentum across the whole community. I hope more researchers and developers will jump in and work on it.

This article appears in the April 2022 print issue as “Andrew Ng, AI Minimalist.”.

Up first is “Being Heumann,” which tells the true story of how Judy Heumann led a 1977 protest that resulted in the longest occupation of a federal building in US history.

The movie is directed by Siân Heder, whose previous film, “CODA,” earned Apple its first Academy Award for Best Picture, in addition to winning Best Adapted Screenplay for Heder and Best Supporting Actor for Troy Kotsur.

The premiere of “Being Heumann” also marks the debut of Apple TV’s new sign language accessibility feature, which allows viewers to watch select titles with an American Sign Language (ASL) or British Sign Language (BSL) interpreter appearing in the corner of the screen.

In addition to “Being Heumann,” the feature is also available for “F1 The Movie,” with “Greyhound” and “Way of the Warrior Kid” gaining support later this year. The latter premieres November 25.

Watch the trailer for “Being Heumann”:.

Watch “Being Heumann” on Apple TV.

The first two episodes of Apple’s anticipated heist thriller series “12 12 12” are now available.

Starring Anthony Mackie (Captain America: Brave New World) and Jamie Dornan (Belfast), the series also features Patrick Fabian (Better Call Saul) and Kali Reis (True Detective: Night Country), among others.

Here’s Apple TV on the newly introduced show, which will release new episodes every Friday through December 25:.

Recent findings suggest that each episode of “12 12 12” unfolds across three timelines of a heist: the 12 months of planning, the 12 hours of the heist and the 12 days following it. The series follows a disgraced FBI agent (Anthony Mackie) and an American career criminal (Jamie Dornan) as they play a zero-sum game of cat and mouse across Europe. At the center of it all is the daring, epic raid on a bank vault deep beneath the streets of Zurich.

Watch the trailer for “12 12 12”:.

The first of two holiday specials coming to Apple TV this season, “Snoopy Presents: 12 Days of Snoopy” is now also available to stream, the other one being “Fraggle Rock: A Holiday Gift,” which arrives December 4.

The premiere marks the latest release under Apple’s ongoing partnership with Peanuts, and joins a growing collection of original Peanuts productions, alongside classics such as “A Charlie Brown Christmas,” “A Charlie Brown Thanksgiving,” and “It’s the Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown.”.

In fact, “A Charlie Brown Thanksgiving” is free to stream on the platform this weekend, meaning even those without an Apple TV subscription can watch it.

Back to “Snoopy Presents: 12 Days of Snoopy,” it follows Snoopy as he tries to get off Santa’s naughty list in the 12 days leading up to Christmas, learning along the way that “there’s more to Christmas than just getting gifts.”.

Meanwhile, the upcoming Apple TV 4K is also available starting today. It’s powered by the A19 chip, up from the previous model’s A15 Bionic. It also has built-in far-field microphones, so you can now interact with Siri without using the remote.

According to recent reports, the new Apple TV also supports Siri AI, enabling things like world knowledge and personal context requests. It’s worth noting that Siri AI is also coming to the second- and third-generation Apple TV 4K models via a software enhancement.

The other flagship feature of the fresh Apple TV 4K is support for a four-HomePod surround sound system. You need four HomePod (2nd generation) or HomePod mini 2 speakers, arranged in matching pairs at the front and rear of the room.

It has been revealed that read my full review of the latest Apple TV 4K for everything you need to know. The big takeaway, though, is that it costs $299, which may be hard for many shoppers to justify.

I do not require the Siri AI feature since it is unavailable in the EU; as a home hub it would still be valuable – if it works 😅.

When buying from Apple’s Online Store for delivery, the fresh Apple TV 4K is backordered to the first week of December. Most Apple Stores appear to have some availability for walk-in purchases starting today.

On Amazon, the new Apple TV 4K is available for delivery as early as this weekend. You can also buy the new Siri Remote, which has a built-in speaker and Find My Precision Finding support, separately.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, A few days later, I had the Lavazza Tabli in my hands, and everything was right in the world.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that I'm Erin, and welcome to The Coffee Lab Episode 25, the series where we forget coffee snobbery. The Coffee Lab is all about making coffee fun. Join me as I help you kickstart your coffee journey!

Here at The Coffee Lab, I'm always eager to get my hands on the newest and most exciting coffee tech. So when I saw a commercial for the Lavazza Tabli on YouTube, I was instantly smitten. Yes. A commercial worked on me — I was influenced!

In a recent development, A few days later, I had the Lavazza Tabli in my hands, and everything was right in the world. At first, I needed to know how. How did the Lavazza Tabli work? If you're not sure what it does, let me give you a quick introduction: it's a pod machine... that doesn't use pods.

That's right. The Tabli uses 100% coffee "Tabs," shaped like hockey pucks, rather than plastic- or aluminum-encased ground coffee. This coffee is compacted so tightly that it keeps its shape. And don't wrinkle your nose — this coffee tastes genuinely incredible. I'm a hard-to-please coffee snob, and I've been singing the Tabli's praises since I tested it a few weeks ago. Here's why the Lavazza Tabli is one of my favorite coffee makers of 2026 — perhaps ever.

Sources indicate that of course, no one's claiming the Lavazza Tabli can make espresso better than a machine like the Lelit MaraX3, single-origin artisan beans, and a talented barista. That would be outrageous and untrue.

It has been revealed that however, I am claiming that the Lavazza Tabli tastes a thousand times better than the best Keurig — I just tested the Keurig K-Mini Mate, and while it's tiny and easy, I would rather drink instant — and ten times better than the best Nespresso. Obviously, I don't have quantitative data to back that up, but can I interest you in a decibel counter for the volume of "Mmm" noises I made while drinking remarked coffees? Because the Tabli surely would win.

Unlike Nespresso and Keurig, Lavazza has just five "Tab" flavors: espresso intenso, qualita rossa, qualita oro, ristretto, and decaf. My favorite was oro. While Nespresso tastes so much better than Keurig, Nespresso shots are still a touch weak and stale, without the vivaciousness on the palate I look for in espresso.

This inexpensive machine uses compressed pucks of grounds to make some truly tasty coffee — without the wasteful pods.

The Tabli? Oh-so vivacious. So vivacious, in fact, that I would equate it to a party on my tongue. The shot is strong and full-bodied, like any Italian coffee tends to be, but with a delicate sweetness rounding out the mouthful. While the flavor depends on your "Tab", both the oro and the rossa were punchy yet delightfully drinkable.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

I noted this in my review, and I'll say it again, but I do wonder if, in time, Lavazza will introduce some kind of Tab-making machine: a press or compacter of some kind, so you can make your own "Tabs". That would be awesome. Catch me making coffee snobs choke on their espressos when I grind single-origin Yirgacheffe into Lavazza Tabs. Ha!

Sources indicate that like Nespresso and Keurig machines, the Lavazza Tabli requires zero cleanup. Well, unless you count removing a pod drawer and emptying it into your compost/trash as cleanup. I'm not sure I would.

According to recent reports, using the Tabli is as easy as this: pop a pod in, press go, drink coffee, empty drawer. Sure, you should probably clean the pod insert after every use, and you should definitely clean out the pod drawer every day (coffee gets moldy promptly), but in terms of scooping-out-wet-grounds-from-a-portafilter-basket-and-emptying-a-milky-drip-tray cleaning, it's minimal.

Although I adore everything about the Lavazza Tabli, there are still a few things I would recommend being aware of before biting the bullet.

One being the most obvious: the Tabli is only compatible with Lavazza-brand Tabs (for now). These are a dollar a pop, in line with Nespresso's original pods (around $0.90-$1) and cheaper than the Vertuo pods (up to $1.40 in some flavors). Keurig pods are around $0.50-$0.70 — but remember you can't recycle them for free, so you're out of pocket for caring about the planet. Great! Thanks, Keurig. Nothing indicates "There is no planet B" like forcing consumers to pay to recycle the plastic pods you make en masse.

Nespresso original and Keurig pods aren't patented, unlike Vertuo, so third parties can manufacture pods in a whole array of flavors.

The Lavazza Tabli machine itself is patented, which I presume extends to the Tabs themselves (boo! — but I get it). This means, if you buy the Tabli, you're locked into buying Lavazza's Tabs — just like a Nespresso Vertuo.

Right now, Lavazza only offers those five core flavors, so no specialty Tabs like fall favorite pumpkin spice or Christmas classics like eggnog or Irish cream. Of course, you can buy syrups to add to your drinks, but Nespresso makes flavored pods. This might be something worth knowing if you're a flavored coffee fanatic.

Sources indicate that would you try the Lavazza Tabli? Or do you love your Nespresso/Keurig machine too much to part with it?

According to recent reports, I would personally buy the Lavazza Tabli. Oh yeah — I saved the best 'til last. It's just $129. No, not a typo. Yes, $129. This is almost incomprehensibly cheap... in the best way. The Nespresso CitiZ is $265, the Nespresso Pixie is $229, and the Keurig K-Supreme is $169.

Erin Bashford is a senior writer at Tom's Guide, focusing on reviews. She has a Masters in Broadcast and Digital Journalism from the University of East Anglia. As an ex-barista, she knows her way around a coffee machine, and as a music lover, she's constantly chipping away at her dream of having a multi-room home sound system. In her spare time you can find her reading, practising yoga, writing, or stressing over today’s NYT Games.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, that goal also was supposed to set up penalties.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chelsea’s Far East tour ended in farce and confusion with players waiting around for a penalty shoot-out that never happened.

The chaos came at the end of a hard-earned, bad-tempered draw against Malaysian champions Johor Darul Ta’zim, with an own-goal in the 89th minute sparring the west London side’s blushes.

In a recent development, that goal also was supposed to set up penalties. But after minutes of waiting around – and Kevin Campello, Chelsea’s head of first-team operations, saying “it’s written in the contract” – the players walked off the pitch.

Recent findings suggest that that confusion ended a feisty affair in which tensions threatened to boil over and that, at certain points, paid little attention to the “friendly” aspect of the clash with seven yellow cards shown. At one point the visitors’ fresh set-piece coach Austin MacPhee exchanged angry words with some of Johor’s coaching staff. The CFC TV commentary team suggested that the spot-kicks were abandoned because of the match’s heated atmosphere.

Austin MacPhee was ready to throw hands😂 pic.twitter.com/CFDgTOwmxE.

Having played just 24 hours earlier in Jakarta – a 3-0 win over AC Milan – it was no surprise to see Xabi Alonso name a fresh XI, a mixture of players who may well be offloaded before the end of the transfer window, those needing to prove themselves, and youngsters given much-needed game time.

And considering Johor are one game away from setting a new world record of 109 matches unbeaten in the top flight – a run that would surpass the current mark set by Ivorian side Asec Mimosas in the early 1990s – it was also no shock to see the Malaysian team offer a stern, pre-season test for the west Londoners.

It has been revealed that after a good start Chelsea were second best in a first half in which Johor should have been at least two goals to the good. The Malaysian champions controlled the first 45 minutes and were 1-0 up after 14 minutes – a low cross from the left side-footed home by Arif Aiman.

The hosts gave the young, inexperienced Chelsea backline a torrid time, especially on the flanks and Óscar Arribas was guilty of not capitalising on a great chance to double Johor’s lead, his shot after cutting in from the right going wide.

In a recent development, while they looked vulnerable at the back, Chelsea also struggled to keep possession in attack. But they got an equaliser they scarcely deserved after Liam Delap was manhandled to the ground in the box by Kevin Medina. The striker, who may well leave Stamford Bridge before the transfer window slams shut, fired home the spot-kick allowing the visitors to go into the break on level terms.

For the most part, the second half followed a similar pattern to the first – Jofor having the better chances, while tensions on the pitch continued to run high.

It was, however, Chelsea who took the lead after the break, Delap once again scoring from the spot, this time after Jamie Gittens was brought down in the area.

Johor, though, kept on creating, thanks in part to a fairly porous visitors’ backline, and levelled through a deflected Arribas free kick, before going 3-2 up thanks thanks to a well-taken Bérgson strike.

Had it stayed that way Chelsea could have had few complaints. But as the clock approached 90 minutes, the visitors had one last attack. Mykhailo Mudryk, just on as a substitute, delivered a cross from the left that Antonio Glauder could only steer into his own net. That was supposed to set up the penalty shoot-out that did not take place and the chance for one of the sides to claim a hollow victory.

According to recent reports, considering a raft of changes and that fact this was far from the first XI, it is hard to know what to make of this. But among the positive things Alonso could take from the game was the impressive form of Nicolas Jackson and good centre-forward play of Delap. The negative was, however, a poor defensive display.

Chelsea return to Stamford Bridge on Saturday for their last pre-season friendly, against Real Sociedad, before the Premier League season starts away at local rivals Fulham on August 24.

Substitutes: Abad, Davies, Hidalgo, Nahuel Leiva, Lowry, Mohamadou Sumareh, Stuart Wilkin.Booked: Israfilov, Antonio Glauder, Silva.Goals: Arif Aiman (14), Arribas (65), Bérgson (86).Chelsea: Sharman-Lowe (Slolina 46); Subuloye, Adarabioyo, Anselmino (Watson 29); Geovany Quenda, Dario Essugo, Nicoll-Jazuli, Gittens (Mudryk 87); Estêvão, Delap, Jacskon (Satpaev 86). Substitutes: Curd, Diakite, Kavuma-McQueen, Sarr, Walsh.Booked: Estêvão, Delap, Jackson, Geovany Quenda, Watson.Goals: Delap (42 pen, 62 pen), Antonio Glauder (89 og).

There will NOT be a penalty shootout. No one is quite sure why.

The commentators on CFC TV are now not so sure!

That was an entertaining pre-season friendly. There was a bit of niggle and that added to the action.

In a recent development, worrying signs at the back, however, for Alonso. Will Chelsea go to four at the back after the break?

The answer to that question (see last post) was so very nearly yes...

Jackson plays in a peach of a through ball with the outside of his right foot, Delap is one-on-one with the keeper and looks for all the world as though he has to score. BUT he scuffs his shot wide.

There will be three minutes of added time. Can Chelsea head into the break with an unexpected lead?

Industry observers note that free-kick for Chelsea on the JDT byline. The ball is put deep into the box, it’s headed back by Tosin before the ball is blazed over the bar.

A minute later Tosin then let’s fly form 25 yards, the ball goes well over the bar.

The hosts should have been more than 1-0 to the good and now they’re drawing. Goals change matches...

Having won the penalty Delap fires the spotkick home, sending the keeper the the wrong way.

Penalty to Chelsea and it’s all thanks to good centre-forward play by Delap. He gets the ball in the box and Medina manhands him to the ground. The referee doesn’t hesitate before pointing to the spot.

Chelsea have struggled to create anything since the opening 15 minutes. They have no control at the front and none at the back at the moment.

According to recent reports, as I type that JDT have another good chance to turn the 1-0 lead into a 2-0 lead. Arribas, whose been a menace all game, dances toward the Chelsea box before delaying the pass too long.

JDT are finding a lot of joy on the flanks, there are three at the back for Chelsea and on the outside are two youngsters. The hosts are working the space well.

Recent findings suggest that yet again Chelsea are made to look decidedly average. A simple ball over the top on the right opens up the visitors’ defence and Arribas is in on goal, he cuts in and lets fly with his left peg, the shot going wide.

That should have been 2-0 to the Malaysian powerhouses.

Worrying signs for Chelsea who have struggled to keep possession up top and looked vulnerable at the back.

Yet more good work from JDT who are being given space by Chelsea. Marcos Guilherme slaloms into the west Londoners’ box and Tosin again doesn’t look the most assured but the JDT player cuts the ball back and the visitors can clear the danger.

Another good attack from the hosts who get in a shot in on goal, it’s deflected and loops into the grateful arms of Sharman-Lowe in the Chelsea goal.

Industry observers note that there’s a break in play with Anselmino down and suffering what looks like a hamstring injury. He is eventually replaced by Reggie Watson.

Meanwhile, the home fans are in fine voice and waving several HUGE flags.

Sources indicate that yep, everyone’s least favourite part of the World Cup in the U, S of A is back. To be fair it’s humid in Johor so taking on fluids during the first 45 minutes is no bad idea.

There’s a bit of argy-bargy not really what you should get in a ‘friendly’. There hasn’t been a bad chellenge in the match so far so not sure where that came from...

Yet more good work from the hosts, this time it’s down the right, Arribas getting the better of Anselmino before shooting at the near post - the attempt hitting the side netting.

After a lively start Chelsea have been second best.

Poor defending from the visitors there but the chance was well snapped up by JDT.

Recent findings suggest that lovely break from the hosts. They break down the left at pace, before the ball is threaded through to the back post and Arif Aiman sidefoots into the back of the net with aplomb.

So very nearly an opener for Chelsea. They break at pace thanks to Estevao who drives down the middle before playing in Jackson. The striker cuts in from the left and shoots, the attempt is saved well by Hamzi and Estevao’s follow up is wide. Is a goal coming?

Recent findings suggest that free-kick for Chelsea some 35 yards out. Too far fro a shot on goal? Of course it is. The ball is floated into the box and the visitors earn a corner.

According to recent reports, what can they create from this set piece? ‘Not much’ is the initial answer as the ball is cleared by JDT but Chelsea win possession back and the ball is fed to Estevao on the left, the Brazilian goes for go with his trusty left peg but the bal goes high and wide.

JDT attack down the left, it’s a lovely ball in that forces a fine header to clear the danger from Adarabioyo.

It has been revealed that no sooner had I sent that last post than Chelsea break through the middle. The ball is fed through to Delap who gets a left-footed shot in on goal forcing a good save from the JDT keeper Hamzi.

Quiet, low-key start to the match. No real shock there, it is a pre-season friendly.

Recent findings suggest that JDT give the ball away in their half and Chelsea have a half-decent platform to launch an attack from. They cannot fashion a chance and also lose possession.

Recent findings suggest that they’re under way in southern Malaysia, Chelsea are in their vibrant blue and the hosts are wearing a fetching pink number. There was a late change for the visitors, Mamadou Sarr has been replaced by Olutayo Subuloye.

We’re moments away from kick-off.

CHELSEA XI TO FACE JOHOR: Sharman-Lowe; Sarr, Tosin, Anselmino; Quenda, Nicoll-Jazuli, Essugo (c), Gittens; Estevao; Jackson, Delap; subs: Slonina, Curd, Subuloye, Diakite, Watson, Mudryk, Walsh, Kavuma-McQueen, Satpayev.

...Luis Garcia. The Spaniard has history with Chelsea, remember the ‘ghost goal’?

Arriving for duty! 🫡 pic.twitter.com/M2XEkLC18n.

Your Chelsea side today! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/0OvvGVmgpc.

A mixture of players who may well be offloaded before the end of the transfer window, those needing to prove themselves, and youngsters you may not have heard of.

Johor Darul Ta’Zim – more commonly known as JDT – are the Man Utd of Malaysia (at least that’s according to a Malaysian friend of mine). In 2013, they were going nowhere and were the dictionary definition of a stagnant club, low on confidence and trophies. That was until the Crown Prince bought the club and, over the next 13 years, transformed it into the powerhouse it is today.

As if to underline JDT’s dominance over Malaysian football they are one game away from the world record unbeaten run in a top flight. The new season of the Malaysian Super League gets under way later this month and should they avoid defeat in their opening match they will extend their unbeaten run - which began in April 2021 - to 109 games and surpass the world record set by Ivorian side Asec Mimosas in the early 1990s.

Chelsea’s pre-season tour of South East Asia ends today with a match against Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia. The clash comes barely 24 hours after the west Londoners beat AC Milan 3-0 in Jakarta, a much-needed win coming on the back of defeats against Juventus and Tottenham.

A fine volley from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to victory in the Indonesian capital.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

Alonso’s side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

Today, the west London side face Malaysian powerhouses Johor at the Sultan Ibrahim Stadium, more on them later, but considering the tight turnaround from yesterday’s match today’s clash will provide a stern test.

“The idea, with the game against Milan and then one in Johor, was to arrive at this weekend with players not being ready for 90 minutes until now,” Alonso explained after the win in Jakarta.

“We wanted to have a logical progression in their loads; so we had our plan and we’ve stuck to that.

In a recent development, “We have another idea [against Johor]; that was decided yesterday [Friday]. The idea is that many young players were coming to have chances to play tomorrow. If not, we’d have been short, as playing two games in two days is quite intense. So we will need them.”.

Stay here for all the team news and action with kick-off set for 1pm.
