    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Arsenal suffered back-to-back pre-season defeats as they lost 3-2 to Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup on Sunday.
    • The loss to the German side followed a 3-1 defeat by Real Betis on Wednesday night in Dublin.
    • Before kick-off, Bruno Guimarães was paraded to the Arsenal faithful after completing his £75m move from Newcastle on Saturday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Arsenal suffered back-to-back pre-season defeats as they lost 3-2 to Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup on Sunday.

    The loss to the German side followed a 3-1 defeat by Real Betis on Wednesday night in Dublin.

    Before kick-off, Bruno Guimarães was paraded to the Arsenal faithful after completing his £75m move from Newcastle on Saturday.

    But enthusiasm about the Brazilian’s arrival was dampened when Dortmund took the lead at the Emirates inside the opening 10 minutes. Felix Nmecha’s incisive pass into the penalty area was met by the run of Samuele Inácio, who made no mistake with a clinical finish into the far corner.

    The Bundesliga side doubled their lead just before the half-hour mark as 18-year-old Greek international Konstantinos Karetsas curled one in from the edge of the box.

    Ten minutes after half-time, Arsenal pulled a goal back through Ethan Nwaneri, who scored from Christos Tzolis’s cross. However, moments later Dortmund restored their two-goal advantage as Joane Gadou smashed home from a corner.

    It has been revealed that arsenal kept their hopes alive through a Viktor Gyokeres penalty after Tzolis was brought down, but Dortmund were able to hold on to claim victory. After the full-time whistle, there was a penalty shoot-out, which Arsenal won 5-4.

    It has been revealed that arsenal still have a number of players to return to action following their World Cup exploits, including Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke. England and Real Madrid midfielder Jude Bellingham was in attendance at the Emirates to watch his younger brother Jobe in action for Dortmund.

    As well as Guimarães, there was another addition on display at the Emirates: Arsenal have added last year’s title win to the list of honours displayed inside the stadium.

Their dream was to overthrow the established powers in English football, and the capture of Guimarães was regarded as a sign that they were truly ready to challenge teams of Arsenal’s stature and wealth.

I just felt inside of me that I need a new challenge in my life and I think to be an Arsenal player is going to be an exciting challenge in my life.

    Industry observers note that premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup. Arsenal beat Spanish side Athletic Bilbao 3-0 in the 2025 edition, with goals from Viktor Gyokeres, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz sealing victory. These sides met during the 2014/15 Champions League group stages, with both games being won 2-0 by the home side.

    Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 just over a week ago but fell to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night. Reflecting on that defeat, Mikel Arteta expressed his frustration at the way his side conceded the goals.

    It has been revealed that “I am disappointed with the result,” Arteta told Arsenal’s in-house media. “We are here to win football matches. We had some fantastic moments in the first half, the way we played, the way we opened them up. We have to score first, clearly, in the two chances that we had before the score.

    “I am very disappointed in the manner that we conceded the first goal, the two giveaways leading to the other two goals. It is true that the finishing quality from them was exceptional, but to win a football match, you have to compete at a different level, especially in those areas of the pitch and that is the learning from today [last Wednesday].”.

    This is in fact Arsenal’s first game at the Emirates since being crowned Premier League champions, as they sealed the title with a game to spare, with that final match of last season being away at Crystal Palace. After today, Arsenal have two more games, including the Community Shield in a week’s time, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

    Dortmund, led by Niko Kovac, finished second in the Bundesliga last season, 16 points off winners Bayern Munich. They have played four pre-season friendlies thus far, winning twice and losing twice. The likes of Karim Adeyemi, Julian Brandt and Niklas Sule have left the club this summer.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that A growing number of people are asking AI chatbots about their health concerns, raising two major concerns: safety and privacy. Apple is now offering a safer way to do this through an Apple Health AI Usage Study.

    This is actually one of Apple’s research studies, but those volunteering to take part in it will be able to ask health questions – with three key assurances not guaranteed by other AI chatbots ….

    In a recent development, apple debuted its Research app back in 2019 with the goal of allowing customers to help universities and medical institutions with health studies. You typically agree to share certain anonymized information from the Apple Health app in order to provide data that can advance medical research. You may also be asked to complete questionnaires.

    Recent findings suggest that the Apple Health AI Usage Study is one of these, but it works in a somewhat different way. You’ll still be invited to share some of your health data, but will also be able to ask an AI system questions about your health.

    Industry observers note that when you ask health questions of a typical AI chatbot, you don’t know how reliable those answers may be or what will happen to your data. Apple study offers three assurances:.

    Apple claims that answers will be generated by the same platform used by healthcare professionals.

    The study is conducted in collaboration with OpenEvidence, a leading clinical AI platform widely used by healthcare professionals that generates answers using medical information from established sources such as The New England Journal of Medicine, Journal of the American Medical Association, and Nature.

    The answers provided to you will include links to peer-reviewed clinical citations.

    As you’d expect from Apple, there are strong privacy protections, including the assurance that your data will not be used to train AI models.

    The study is designed from the ground up with privacy protections, transparency, and clinical guardrails, and study data will not be used to train AI models. Participants retain control over whether to share any HealthKit metrics or survey responses, and Apple has implemented security measures to protect the study data it maintains, as well as the confidentiality of participants’ information.

    CNET reports on Apple’s assurance that none of your chats will be retained.

    OpenEvidence will delete both question and response data within 24 hours. A small group of Apple researchers will have access to coded versions of survey responses, separated from personally identifiable information, summaries of conversations and categories of the most common conversation types.

    It has been revealed that access to the study is at the moment limited to consumers in the US by downloading the app. If you try it, please do share your thoughts in the comments.

    #3901. Apple’s first smart glasses are finally taking shape — here are 3 major ways it will stand out

    Apple’s first smart glasses are finally taking shape — here are 3 major ways it will stand out

    📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (858 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomsguide

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that the worst-kept secret in Cupertino is finally spilling out onto the timeline.
    • According to recent reports, back in 2025, I wrote that visionOS was quietly setting the stage for a killer pair of smart specs — completely sidestepping the bulky, overpriced Apple Vision Pro.
    • Sounds like a home run on paper, but there are some significant obstacles between now and WWDC to overcome — not just in Apple’s software, but in smart eyewear more broadly.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that the worst-kept secret in Cupertino is finally spilling out onto the timeline. According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, Apple is targeting WWDC 2027 to launch its first pair of smart glasses.

    According to recent reports, back in 2025, I wrote that visionOS was quietly setting the stage for a killer pair of smart specs — completely sidestepping the bulky, overpriced Apple Vision Pro. Well, turns out that prediction was dead on, as a stripped down version of the OS and an older Apple Watch chip will be packed into a frame thinner than the Ray-Ban Metas.

    Sounds like a home run on paper, but there are some significant obstacles between now and WWDC to overcome — not just in Apple’s software, but in smart eyewear more broadly.

    Sources indicate that the most exciting detail about the prototype (codenamed N50) isn’t that “Tic Tac” sized MagSafe charger or the flushed oval cameras — it’s that native Wi-Fi connectivity. Up until this point, anyone wearing smart glasses will know the Bluetooth tether is their Achilles’ heel.

    In a recent development, wearables are supposed to gain you freedom from your phone, and you can’t really do that if you rely on something you have to be close to. The moment you walk into another room leaving your phone on your desk, that wearable turns into a pair of dumb specs.

    But by giving the glasses their own Wi-Fi radio, Apple could be granting you actual independence. That friction of leaving your phone on the charger at home and still streaming audio/pinging Siri would be a huge quality-of-life upgrade. The closest we’re getting to this is the cellular data plan in Snap Specs at the moment.

    Industry observers note that my initial prediction was based on the idea that visionOS is a visual experience. “Vision” is in the name after all, but if you were hoping for AR displays, you’re going to have to keep waiting. According to Gurman, Apple’s first glasses will be a screen-free experience.

    Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

    With audio and cameras in the driving sign, the glasses will use visual intelligence to scan your surroundings and Siri AI to answer questions about it, all while relying on built-in mics and speakers for calls and Apply Music playback.

    Of course, one of the key benefits here is that by ditching the heavy optical engines, Apple gets to keep the glasses lightweight, stylish and comfortable. But also, this design choice creates a massive, singular issue: the future of this category needs a screen (in my opinion).

    And this brings me to the elephant in the room. Apple is betting the entire farm on Siri, but Siri’s not ready yet.

    In a recent development, the master blueprint is Siri being the agentic bridge of your devices. Instead of developers building dedicated apps for the glasses, your assistant will just hijack your existing iOS apps — booking Ubers, ordering Starbucks or securing OpenTable reservations entirely through conversation.

    Sources indicate that in theory, it’s brilliant. In practice, it could be a very tough hill to climb.

    Sources indicate that between now and 2027, Siri AI needs to get so much better. Currently, we’re seeing long pause times to simple prompts on your iPhone, and the Apple HomeView routinely fumbles complex, multi-step smart home commands.

    If Siri is currently struggling to seamlessly manage a stationary smart home, imagine how badly it is going to hallucinate when you’re walking down a noisy Manhattan street asking it to visually analyze a restaurant menu and cross-reference your calendar.

    Sources indicate that gurman’s report already notes that Apple’s software and AI development is running behind schedule, which could easily delay this 2027 launch. And honestly? They should until it’s bulletproof.

    In a recent development, apple’s hardware team looks set to deliver a sleek, Wi-Fi-enabled wearable showpiece. But if they strap it to an AI assistant that still doesn’t understand what you actually want, that expensive pair of smart glasses is going to feel like a very expensive bluetooth headset.

    According to recent reports, and that’s before even looking at the usability of these agentic flows. Uber reported that AI agents only booked four rides in a week. Four. And there are many more examples. Adoption just isn’t there right now. That’s not to say it shouldn’t happen, but it will take a far smarter Siri graduating to a true agent to make it worthwhile.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's debt buyback announcement this week fits into a broader pattern that can signal a forthcoming crisis, according to billionaire investor Ray Dalio.

    Sources indicate that the Bridgewater Associates founder said Bessent's strategy to increase government debt purchases may portend trouble for the U.S. economy. Coupled with the Japanese government reducing its U.S. bond market exposure and surging long-dated American bond yields, Dalio said investors may want to prepare their portfolios for increased risk by owning cryptocurrencies and gold.

    "I am confident that the government's financial condition is at an inflection point," Dalio wrote in a LinkedIn post published Friday. "If this is not dealt with now, the debts will build up to levels where they can't be managed without great trauma.".

    Recent findings suggest that dalio noted that the Treasury Department has "only limited capacity" to buy back bonds. Bessent told CNBC on Thursday that his team was going to "make a market" and that the purchases would likely top $4 billion.

    In a recent development, the U.S. is spending about 40% more than it's bringing in, resulting in the burgeoning budget deficit, Dalio mentioned. The U.S. budget deficit topped $432 billion in July, but Bessent told CNBC that it's likely peaked under President Donald Trump's administration.

    Sources indicate that bessent stated in the interview that a team was looking at ways to shrink spending by hundreds of billions of dollars. But Dalio said there is "very little ability" to do so given that it is either committed or considered essential.

    After years of overspending, Dalio said total debt now dwarfs what the U.S. brings in each year. If the U.S. government was a business, Dalio said debt service payments would come in at roughly $11 trillion — about 200% of annual revenue.

    Dalio, 77, warned the cost of repaying principal and servicing the debt will only grow over time.

    Sources indicate that to solve this, Dalio stated the U.S. needs to carefully employ a three-part strategy to get the budget deficit down to 3% of gross domestic product.

    According to recent reports, first, Dalio noted the U.S. government needs to reduce its spending. Second, he said tax revenue needs to be raised. Finally, the Latest York native and Harvard Business School alumni said lower interest rates were needed.

    Industry observers note that "All three need to happen concurrently so as to prevent any one from being too large," Dalio noted. "If any one is too large, the adjustment will be traumatic.".

    Dalio cautioned against ramming through these adjustments by "force." For instance, "it would be very bad if the Federal Reserve unnaturally forced interest rates down," he mentioned.

    Dalio said it's important to to take steps now, while the economy is healthy. An economy in recession requires increased government spending, he said.

    Sources indicate that dalio noted the exact timing of a debt crisis can be swayed by variables ranging from military conflict to political change. On its current trajectory, the U.S. could enter such a crisis in as early as one year or as late as five. "My guess, which I suppose will be a bad one, is that it will come in three years, give or take two, if the course we're on is not changed.".

    To prepare, Dalio recommended investors are underweight debt assets, such as bonds.

    As much as 10% to 15% of a portfolio could land in gold, as well as "a bit" of bitcoin, the hedge fund founder stated.

    Dalio's post came at the tail end of a volatile week for U.S. financial markets. Rising long-term Treasury yields have pressured stocks, leading the S&P 500 to snap a a three-week-long advance.

    A leaker today says that the iPhone 20 Pro is getting a latest and more sophisticated sensor for the main camera, but details are unclear ….

    It has been revealed that there are two main reasons people still buy standalone cameras despite having an iPhone in their pocket wherever they go. The first is lens quality: iPhones have small plastic lenses compared to the far larger and more sophisticated glass lenses used with dedicated cameras.

    The second is sensor size. All other things being equal, a larger sensor will capture more light and provide a higher quality image. Current smartphone sensors are absolutely tiny compared to those used in even mid-range consumer cameras.

    We’ve seen two previous reports suggesting that a larger sensor is on the way for future iPhones. One of these suggested that it would be coming in 2027 or 2028, although a later one suggested the latter date was more likely.

    The reports were not without a catch, however, suggesting that the larger sensor would only be for the telephoto lens and would have a 200MP resolution. Squeezing more pixels into a given sensor size tends to sacrifice low light capabilities in return for higher resolution. This is less likely to be an matter with a telephoto lens, which is normally used outdoors rather than inside.

    Industry observers note that what I’d really love to see is a significantly larger sensor for the main camera, with no increase in resolution. This would improve low light performance and overall image quality.

    Microsoft outage saw 80% of servers fail – here’s what happened

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that last week saw a truly epic outage to Microsoft 365, with a huge number of people unable to send and receive emails.
    • Microsoft has now explained what went wrong, stating that the mistake that led to the failure was actually made all the way back in July without being detected ….
    • In a recent development, the manufacturer mentioned at the time that it was a technical matter and not a cyber attack, and that it was working hard to fix the problem, admitting that it was taking longer than expected.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that last week saw a truly epic outage to Microsoft 365, with a huge number of people unable to send and receive emails. The company has now admitted that at the worst point, more than 80% of its servers were unresponsive.

    Microsoft has now explained what went wrong, stating that the mistake that led to the failure was actually made all the way back in July without being detected ….

    In a recent development, the manufacturer mentioned at the time that it was a technical matter and not a cyber attack, and that it was working hard to fix the problem, admitting that it was taking longer than expected. Microsoft also denied that it was related to the thousands of layoffs unveiled the previous month.

    Customers were understandably unimpressed at the scale of the outage and the time taken to fix it, although meme creators were having fun.

    Recent findings suggest that sorry but you have to be change the name now. Thems the rules pic.twitter.com/5UttZ8nt9f.

    It certainly points out that when you base your business on cloud services, you also take the risk that comes with that.

    Platform head Charles Lamanna admitted the severity of the problem.

    Recent findings suggest that in less than two hours, the previously unknown defect was encountered across our fleet and rendered them unresponsive. At its lowest, more than 80% of servers were unresponsive.

    He remarked it resulted from a combination of two complications. The company maintains two independent network gateway systems, one of which failed, meaning that the remaining gateway took the full load. That wouldn’t have been a problem on its own, Microsoft stating that each one has enough capacity to handle all traffic. However, a mistake made back in July led to a cascading failure.

    A latent defect caused servers to become overwhelmed and unresponsive under certain load conditions. This was due to lock contention inside an internal process which caused the machine to become unavailable. This defect was the result of a fix that was prepared specifically for Microsoft 365 networking gateway servers […].

    The initial change in behavior first started deployment in July of this year. The patch went through safe deployment and saturated globally over several weeks, during which time no challenges were observed. For more than three months, the change was deployed worldwide without impact. Our normal load testing did not detect the latent concern because the different traffic and SKU mix used in our test labs. The contention issue is worsened on machines with more cores and newer hardware; whereas our load testing tended to focus on our weaker hardware SKUs with fewer cores.

    In other words, the patch wasn’t tested under the conditions in which it was most likely to fail.

    In a recent development, while the organization claims that the incident is unrelated to laying off staff and replacing them with AI systems, I find myself extremely skeptical. It seems inconceivable that a company of Microsoft’s size could make what appears to be a schoolboy error of this magnitude unless there were insufficient engineers working on the update. Please share your own thoughts in the comments.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • We’re excited to announce Aristotle’s expansion into Rust, one of the fastest-growing programming languages for high-stakes software.
    • Recent findings suggest that the expansion builds on Aristotle’s support of C and Verilog and marks a major advancement in our mission to verify all code.
    • With support for Rust, Aristotle can prove that your code has no undefined behavior and does exactly what its spec claims, even inside unsafe blocks.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    We’re excited to announce Aristotle’s expansion into Rust, one of the fastest-growing programming languages for high-stakes software.

    Recent findings suggest that the expansion builds on Aristotle’s support of C and Verilog and marks a major advancement in our mission to verify all code. Instead of relying on testing to catch every flaw, developers can now use Aristotle to prove their Rust code works as intended before it ships, providing a fresh level of certainty to systems where even a single bug can be catastrophic.

    With support for Rust, Aristotle can prove that your code has no undefined behavior and does exactly what its spec claims, even inside unsafe blocks. If you’re rewriting C in Rust, it can prove the new code behaves the same as the original.

    “Rust is where much of the world’s most critical new code is being written, and increasingly, AI is the one writing it,” stated our CEO Tudor Achim. “With Aristotle, organizations can now prove their code does exactly what it’s supposed to, from the smart contracts that move money to the infrastructure that keeps systems running.”.

    Industry observers note that rust powers software across mission-critical industries, from cloud computing and cybersecurity to automotive, aerospace, and financial services including crypto. It’s the backbone of Solana’s smart contracts that drive trading, lending, payments, and other DeFi services on the Solana blockchain.

    Recent findings suggest that these systems have no room for error. Smart-contract transactions can’t be undone, so a single missed bug is all attackers need to drain hundreds of millions of dollars. Instead of relying on slow, manual audits that are outdated immediately after they’re published, Aristotle runs on every fresh line of code, proving it behaves as intended across all possible inputs and catching critical flaws before code goes live.

    You can see it on real Solana programs. On Manifest, an open-source order book, Aristotle proved 28 results across the whole order book, including that a valid swap goes through, and found a rounding bug the team has since fixed. At Project 0, a prime broker, it proved the books stay consistent through deposits, withdrawals, borrows, repayments, and liquidations, in any order.

    To bring that protection to more developers, we’re partnering with the Solana Foundation to support established Solana programs and help new builders verify their smart contracts.

    “When software moves real money, security has to keep pace with every code change,” said Ludo Galabru at the Solana Foundation. “Aristotle makes formal verification more accessible to Solana developers, helping teams check critical properties of their programs before launch and keep verifying them with every revision.”.

    According to recent reports, aristotle for Rust is available today. Get started at aristotle.harmonic.fun with self-serve, consumption-based pricing, or contact bd@harmonic.fun for volume pricing, dedicated support, and custom deployment.

    Press inquiries: pr@harmonic.fun.

It’s quite similar to the t61, but a little smaller and lighter. I was worried that the smaller part would be a problem, but I’ve gotten used to it. I really like the fact that it’s much lighter than my old t42. It just makes it seem so much more usable on the go. Lugging out the t42 was always a chore.

    Anyway, I was at the Office 2.0 conference today, where I was giving a little presentation on the Techdirt Insight Community, and about an hour before the presentation, I went to find a quiet place to practice the presentation… and discovered that my brand latest laptop wouldn’t work. I knew something was wrong when the “sleep” light wasn’t lit. I started to get worried when I plugged in the laptop and the battery light didn’t light up. Then I noticed that even though the machine had been asleep, it was really really hot. Pushing the power button did nothing. No lights were on and nothing seemed to get them to turn on. I pulled out the battery and put it back in and that did nothing as well.

    So I called up IBM support and explained the situation. The guy on the other end then let me in on the secret power button code to revive your dead Thinkpad. After assessing the situation (totally dead laptop) he warned me: “Okay, this is going to sound totally bizarre, but I want you to give this a try…” He then had me unplug the AC adapter and take out the battery. Then, you push the power button 10 times in a row at one second intervals. Next, you push and hold the power button for 30 seconds. Then you put the battery back in and push the power button… and she lives. The computer came back, good as ever.

    Recent findings suggest that I asked the guy what the power button pushing incantation did and he noted “static discharge” so apparently there was some sort of static that caused a short or something. I tried to get the guy to explain in more detail what happened, but he said “dude, you know as much as I do… but your machine is working.”.

    So, if you happen to have a Thinkpad that suddenly drops completely dead for no reason, try the power button trick.

    Forget up, up, down, down, left, right, left, right, B, A. This little code is now the coolest “cheat” code I know….

    Sources indicate that I think 2Smart is right. It’s not entirely uncommon for one to have to press the power button once or twice with no power attached to release the residual charge built up in capacitors. When the unit attempts to start it will use up the remaining power in the unsuccessful attempt. From there, you can sometimes start the machine. A common manifestation of this problem is fans spinning but no display. This can manifest after a power outage or other unexpected shut down.

    According to recent reports, 1st off this works on any laptop/model not just think-pad. This isn’t a magic trick, the point of this besides the static discharge, this resets the Bios of computer by pulling all the charge out of the Internal 2032 CMOS Battery, which in return reboots the BIOS. This can happen for many reason not just a static charge, Some computers can have a bad infection that activates when the computer goes to sleep mode, this is a well known attacker, then the virus proceeds to overload your machine to shut down thus causing the bios to have the command programmed to stay shut down. Well by doing the manual BIOS RESET such as this, resets the configurations in the bios back to default.

    Also you can try pulling battery out, unplugging charger, and then hold power button for 1 minute if the 10X an 30sec hold doesn’t work for you. And if for some reason it still don’t work, removing the 2032 CMOS Battery on the MOBO for 1 minute or replace it, the battery which is usually located near the RAM on most laptops, not all have the battery located in same place, I suggest if you need to go that far google your model of computer to locate the internal CMOS Battery.

    Wine Computer Repair & Security.

    Industry News: HomeView missing some podcast feeds? Here’s why

    📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (253 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: 9to5mac

    ⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Apple’s latest HomeView features the Podcasts app, but not all feeds appear to be supported for now.
    • tvOS 27.0 added playback support for HLS-based video podcasts on Apple TV 4K’s Podcasts app.
    • The same patch introduced a bug that dropped support for syncing indicates manually added via URL.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Apple’s latest HomeView features the Podcasts app, but not all feeds appear to be supported for now. Instead, HomeView appears to have the same bug that tvOS 27 introduced to the Apple TV 4K’s Podcasts app.

    tvOS 27.0 added playback support for HLS-based video podcasts on Apple TV 4K’s Podcasts app.

    The same patch introduced a bug that dropped support for syncing indicates manually added via URL.

    The new Apple HomeView appears to have this same bug. Video podcasts using HLS technology are supported, but indicates added via URL do not work.

    As of tvOS 27.3 beta 1, the bug is still present on Apple TV 4K 2nd-gen and newer.

    Because tvOS 27 doesn’t run on Apple TV 4K 1st-gen, URL-based subscriptions still work in the Podcasts app — just not HLS-based video feeds.

    Anyway, if you’re missing certain feeds in the Podcasts app on HomeView, this is likely the reason.

    Top Wall Street analysts believe in the growth potential of these 3 stocks

    📅 23 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (909 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, geopolitical uncertainty in the Middle East and soaring bond yields weighed on global markets this past week.
    • Despite those continued challenges, top Wall Street analysts are bullish on the prospects of several stocks due to their long-run growth potential and exposure to lucrative business lines, including AI.
    • Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, geopolitical uncertainty in the Middle East and soaring bond yields weighed on global markets this past week. And investors are closely assessing the valuations of artificial intelligence stocks amid concerns about the sustainability of high spending on AI infrastructure.

    Despite those continued challenges, top Wall Street analysts are bullish on the prospects of several stocks due to their long-run growth potential and exposure to lucrative business lines, including AI.

    Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Sources indicate that cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike Holdings (CRWD) is this week's first stock pick. The company is scheduled to announce fiscal second-quarter results on August 26.

    Ahead of Q2 FY27 earnings, Truist analyst Junaid Siddiqui reiterated a buy rating on CrowdStrike stock and raised his price target to $245 from $187.50. Following CrowdStrike's impressive fiscal first-quarter performance and guidance raise, Siddiqui expects another strong quarter.

    According to recent reports, the 5-star analyst's optimism is backed by continued strength in Falcon Flex adoption and encouraging large deal activity. Siddiqui also cited continued momentum across emerging products. With the FY27 outlook assuming persistent strength in CrowdStrike's net fresh annual recurring revenue (ARR), Siddiqui is more focused on the longevity of key growth catalysts such as Falcon Flex adoption, platform consolidation and AI-led demand.

    The analyst highlighted that talks with partners were encouraging, with pipeline generation and momentum in large deals remaining healthy in the fiscal second quarter despite tough, year-over-year comparisons.

    "We continue to view CrowdStrike as one of the primary beneficiaries of platform consolidation, though we expect investors to remain focused on competitive dynamics and whether current growth levels represent a latest baseline or a period of demand acceleration," the analyst mentioned.

    Recent findings suggest that siddiqui ranks No. 226 among more than 12,400 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 80% of the time, delivering an average return of about 40%. See CrowdStrike Financials on TipRanks.

    According to recent reports, shares of personal computer maker Dell Technologies (DELL) have rallied 251% this year, driven by strong demand for AI servers. Recently, Evercore analyst Amit Daryanani reiterated a buy rating on DELL and raised his price target to $550 from $500.

    The 5-star analyst contends that while Dell's AI compute segment is getting investors' attention, the company's Storage business is underappreciated and well-positioned to drive revenue and profit acceleration. Daryanani expects the storage business to see higher demand once enterprises start to bring workload back on-premises.

    It has been revealed that the analyst highlighted that Dell's Storage business, estimated to account for only 10% of FY27 revenue, is one of the factors that could help improve profit margins, given its higher profitability compared to AI servers. Daryanani estimates that the Storage business's operating margin is currently in the low-20% range, while margins for the AI server and traditional server businesses are in the mid-single-digit and mid-teens range, respectively.

    Overall, Daryanani views the Storage business as an notable catalyst for three reasons: Dell has one of the broadest storage portfolios in the industry; Storage has a significantly higher margin profile than AI servers; and the shift toward proprietary, software-defined storage and AI-focused platforms.

    "We think DELL's storage business is becoming increasingly strategic as AI infrastructure deployments move beyond GPU procurement and toward full stack + AI-ready architectures," stated Daryanani.

    Daryanani ranks No. 19 among more than 12,400 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 71% of the time, delivering an average return of 38.70%. See Dell Technologies Statistics on TipRanks.

    SanDisk (SNDK) is benefiting from AI-driven demand for its memory and storage products. Following the company's 2026 Investor Day event, J.P. Morgan analyst Harlan Sur resumed research coverage of SNDK with a buy rating (it was earlier, "Not Rated") and a price target of $2,250.

    The 5-star analyst believes SanDisk is well-positioned to capitalize on a structural inflection reached in NAND demand, driven by strong growth in AI inference. Sur's bullishness is based on three key factors.

    First, Sur believes that SanDisk's Upcoming Business Model (NBM) framework (or long-term agreements) has enhanced its margin profile and reduced cyclicality. SNDK's eight signed NBMs represent a total contract value of $94 billion and a gross margin of about 80%, even at the floor pricing.

    Sources indicate that second, Sur highlighted the growing NAND market and expects the total addressable market to surge from about $70 billion in calendar year 2025 to over $300 billion in 2026 and about $500 billion in 2027. Importantly, the analyst noted that data centers are the largest driver of NAND growth, as hyperscalers increasingly deploy flash for AI inference workloads.

    According to recent reports, finally, Sur is optimistic on SanDisk due to its technology dominance. The firm's BiCS10 technology is sampling ahead of schedule and has 65% more bits per wafer than BiCS8, the analyst said. Also, Sur expects SanDisk's High Bandwidth Flash to become a differentiated memory platform for AI inference.

    "Layered on top, mgmt's commitment to returning 100% of excess cash flow to shareholders should drive an aggressive share count reduction trajectory that further amplifies EPS growth on a per-share basis," stated Sur.

    According to recent reports, sur ranks No. 15 among more than 12,400 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 71% of the time, delivering an average return of 43.20%. See SanDisk Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

    According to recent reports, with user permission, ChatGPT Health connects to Apple Health and supported medical records to provide useful context to health-related questions. The feature presently works in the United States on iPhone, iPad, and the web.

    #3880. Tech Report: Squircles

    📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1274 w)

    Tech Report: Squircles

    📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1274 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Linebender

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • A squircle is a shape intermediate between a square and a circle.
    • Recent findings suggest that the best known squircle is the superellipse, popularized by Piet Hein.
    • The superellipse has the formula $|x|^n + |y|^n = 1$ (we’ll use a unit radius for convenience).
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A squircle is a shape intermediate between a square and a circle. There is no single mathematical definition, rather there are a number of curves that fit this shape. All general squircles are parametrized, and can vary between circle and square.

    Loading the interactive tester….

    Recent findings suggest that the best known squircle is the superellipse, popularized by Piet Hein. Martin Gardner wrote a detailed narrative of its origin in a Scientific American column in 1977. The text is replicated in https://piethein.com/superellipse/ but that’s missing equations and figures.

    The superellipse has the formula $|x|^n + |y|^n = 1$ (we’ll use a unit radius for convenience). When $n=2$ it is a circle, and it approaches a square asymptotically as $n \rightarrow \infty$.

    According to recent reports, there is no standard measurement for squircles. For superellipses, the exponent is the most common parameter. A good choice is the coordinates of the midpoint of the quadrant, assuming a unit radius; here $x$ and $y$ are equal. The conversion formula is simple and intuitive: $x = 0.5^{1/n}$. This measurement is called "gauge" in the interactive demo above, and is the primary parameter; with the exception of some unreachable regions of parameter space, it should be possible to compare different squircle variants with similar gauge.

    There are two basic approaches to squircle creation. One is a single analytic curve, where curvature reaches zero at the poles, but is otherwise nonzero. The other is mixing straight line segments with corners. A significant advantage of the latter approach is that it can adapt to rectangles of arbitrary aspect ratio without distorting the corner shape.

    Squircles received renewed attention when Apple changed the icon shape from rounded rectangle to their own squircle in iOS 7 in 2013. There were several blog posts to analyze and recreate the shape. An early analysis suggested that it was a superellipse of exponent 5, but when people extracted the Béziers and looked more closely, that was found to be inaccurate. Rather, it’s a flat-sided squircle.

    Recent findings suggest that for the raw Bézier path data of the Apple shape, the best source is the PaintCode blog. This blog correctly points out some bugs in that logic, and also has some details on behavior for oval rather than square aspect ratios.

    The Apple shape has a number of flaws, including one extraneous straight line segment, and a lack of symmetry. However, those flaws are minor, and really only reveal themselves under close analysis.

    Sources indicate that the Apple shape has no additional parameter, so its variation is controlled entirely by the length of the flat side. With no flat side, it has a gauge fixed at 0.809.

    An extremely detailed analysis of the Apple shape is in The Art of Continuous Corners.

    Figma published a blog post, Desperately Seeking Squircles, with an analysis of the Apple squircle and their own approximation. It is influential because Figma is an important design tool, because their writeup was compelling, and because there are any number of open source implementations of it, mostly TypeScript/JavaScript.

    In a recent development, the Figma blog contains a plot of the Béziers comprising a cleaned up version of iOS 7 rounded rectangle, revealing three Bézier segments per quadrant. It fixes the straight-line segment and the asymmetry, so is not an exact match. The middle segment is very close to an arc. The other segments are more problematic. They have zero curvature at the endpoints, so are G2 continuous with flat sides, but there is a curvature discontinuity with the middle (arc) section, and their curvature profile is not especially smooth. A reasonable guess is that it was drawn by hand to be approximately smooth.

    Without a flat side, the Figma squircle is only capable of a gauge between $\sqrt{0.5}$ (0.707) and 0.854. Gauges up to 1 are of course attainable by adding the flat side.

    Industry observers note that the Figma blog suggests “smoothed curvature profiles” which have a piecewise linear relationship between arc length and curvature. It then goes on to approximate them with cubic Bézier segments, but their approximation has fairly significant curvature discontinuities when joining to the circular arc. The clothoid squircle is worth describing explicitly, as it has G2 continuity (as opposed to G1 for the Figma approximation).

    The behavior is generally similar to the Figma variant. Without a flat side, it is only capable of a gauge between $\sqrt{0.5}$ (0.707) and 0.790.

    Squircles got a significant boost as they’re now standardized in CSS, as the corner-shape property of the box decorations spec. These specify real superellipse corners, with additional tweaks and support for animation.

    It has been revealed that while the CSS spec mandates the actual superellipse shape, practical implementations will generally use a Bézier approximation. A blog post, The corner cases of implementing CSS corner-shape in Blink, gives an efficient closed-form approximation, with two Bézier segments per quadrant. This formula, determined using symbolic regression, is parametrized, and handles exponents 2 and above well. It is exact for placing the midpoint (this is part of the formula), so is well calibrated in that regard.

    Recent findings suggest that the early analysis of the Apple squircle shape as being approximately an exponent 5 superellipse was based on coarse shape only and didn't take into account its flat side. A much better match to the Apple shape is attainable using a superellipse with exponent 3 and a corresponding flat side length to match the gauge. This has G2 continuity and a similar curvature profile. This illustration was made using the Chromium approximation, so it should match the browser.

    In a recent development, here's the CSS to accomplish the "close to Apple" squircle shape. Note that the parameter to the superellipse() function is the base-2 log of the exponent, so the value for an exponent of 3 is 1.585.

    A superellipse of exponent $n$ has continuity $G(\lceil n \rceil - 1)$. This includes the flat-sided variants, as, for exponent > 2, the endpoint of the quadrant has zero curvature. A perfect circle (and indeed, any even integer exponent) without flat sides is of course the exception, as it has an infinitely high order of continuity.

    Recent findings suggest that as a general observation, for visual smoothness, the shape should have G2 continuity. Of the variants discussed, only the clothoid and superellipse (for n > 2) have this property. The Chromium approximation comes close; it doesn't have zero curvature by construction when joining the flat part, but does at the corner join by symmetry (unlike the Figma approximation, which has an additional arc there).

    Quite a number of other curves can be pressed into service as squircles if need be.

    In a recent development, the polynomial spiral (“spiro”) curve can do a reasonable flat-sided squircle with G2 continuity. See the “suitcase corners” section of Raph's thesis, figure 7.2.

    Conic sections (hyperbolas). These approximate a sharp corner but are only G1 continuous (if flat sided).

    Industry observers note that fernández-Guasti squircle, defined by $x^2 + y^2 - s^2x^2y^2 = 1$. This is used in engineering but likely not in graphic design.

    The Wikipedia page on squircles has a “periodic squircle” which has very similar behavior to the Fernández-Guasti one (they are visually near indistinguishable).

    The offset curve of a squircle is not a squircle, but (a) it’s close, and (b) concentric squircles might be visually just as appealing or more so; for example a slightly rounded inner corner might look better than a sharp one if the curvature exceeds the stroke half-width.

    The blurred rounded rectangle approximation is based on applying shading to a superellipse; each iso-line is in fact a superellipse.

    Robert Pattinson is 007 — here’s what we know about the next era of James Bond

    📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (779 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomsguide

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that robert Pattinson is James Bond.
    • In an announcement post on the James Bond website, Pattinson stated, “James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime.
    • Sources indicate that “I'm deeply grateful to Denis [Villeneuve], Amy [Pascal], David [Heyman], Tanya [Lapointe], and everyone at Amazon MGM Studios for their belief in me.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that robert Pattinson is James Bond. Today (Nov. 16), Amazon MGM Studios confirmed it’s found its new 007 in the form of the British actor most known for his roles as Edward Cullen in “Twilight,” Bruce Wayne in Matt Reeves’ “The Batman” series, and for shouting “somebody get these beggars out of here” in Christopher Nolan’s blockbuster megahit “The Odyssey.”.

    In an announcement post on the James Bond website, Pattinson stated, “James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime.

    Sources indicate that “I'm deeply grateful to Denis [Villeneuve], Amy [Pascal], David [Heyman], Tanya [Lapointe], and everyone at Amazon MGM Studios for their belief in me. To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement. I couldn’t be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team.

    Pattinson succeeds Daniel Craig, who bowed out of Bond with 2021’s “No Time to Die,” his fifth outing as the suave superspy. While there is no release date for Pattinson debut as 007, the next installment in the long-running franchise will be directed by Denis Villeneuve, who has already worked with Pattinson on the upcoming “Dune Part 3,” and the next Bond blockbuster will be written by Steven Knight, the creator of “Peaky Blinders.”.

    On the casting news, which has been the subject of intense media and fan speculation, Mike Hopkins, Head of Prime Video & Amazon MGM Studios, remarked, “Today marks a defining moment for our studio and a significant milestone in the history of James Bond as we proudly introduce Robert Pattinson as the next 007.

    “This iconic character has captivated audiences around the world for more than six decades, and there’s no doubt that Robert’s remarkable range, magnetic screen presence, and quiet intensity make him an exceptional choice to carry that legacy forward.”.

    Pattinson is believed to have won out against a competitive field with several other actors under consideration, including Callum Turner, Jack Lowden, Josh O’Connor and Nicholas Hoult.

    Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

    Pattinson will be the seventh actor to portray Ian Fleming's beloved character on the substantial screen in an Eon Productions-produced 007 film. It will be the 26th James Bond movie in the ongoing franchise; the first was 1962's "Dr. No.".

    Recent findings suggest that the James Bond casting rumor mill has been in overdrive in recent weeks. And while the odds-on favorite kept switching (first it was Turner, then Lowden), once Pattinson’s name emerged, the wind was only blowing one way.

    Industry observers note that in many ways, Pattinson was the safe pick. He is the most high-profile star of the names rumored to be in the running, and he has extensive experience working in the Hollywood blockbuster machine, having featured in major franchises like “Twilight,” “Harry Potter” and “The Batman” — the long-delayed sequel to which Pattinson is at the moment filming.

    Industry observers note that however, being the safe pick doesn’t make him the wrong choice, far from it. Pattinson is a guaranteed draw. Earlier this year, alongside Zendaya, he helped drive the off-kilter romantic comedy “The Drama” to $135 million globally, a sign that Pattinson can get butts in seats. His latest movie, “Primetime,” has grossed $62 million worldwide on a sub-$15 million budget.

    More importantly, Pattinson is beloved by a key demographic that Amazon MGM will hope to court with its next Bond movie: younger viewers. The Bond IP goes far with older watchers, but for the franchise to remain at the top of the Hollywood table, it will need to get the TikTok generation watching. Pattinson is the type of actor who can speak to multiple generations.

    So, while some longtime 007 fans will bemoan Amazon’s decision to cast an A-lister instead of taking the approach of Bond’s former stewards, the Broccoli family, by selecting a relative unknown. In 2026, Robert Pattinson looks to tick all the right boxes for a new era of Bond.

    Rory is a Senior Entertainment Editor at Tom’s Guide based in the UK. He covers a wide range of topics but with a particular focus on gaming and streaming. When he’s not reviewing the latest games, searching for hidden gems on Netflix, or writing hot takes on newly introduced gaming hardware, TV reveals and movies, he can be found attending music festivals and getting far too emotionally invested in his favorite football team.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, iOS 27.3 beta 2 is now available, and Apple is adding the ability for owners to unlock higher usage limits for Apple Intelligence and Siri AI via iCloud+.
    • From the start, Apple has noted that some Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features have usage limits because “they rely on powerful server models.” The manufacturer previously outlined that increased access would be available across most iCloud+ subscription plans, and now we have the full details on how this will work.
    • Apple says the new system applies to several categories of Apple Intelligence features, including:.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, iOS 27.3 beta 2 is now available, and Apple is adding the ability for owners to unlock higher usage limits for Apple Intelligence and Siri AI via iCloud+. Here’s everything you need to know.

    From the start, Apple has noted that some Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features have usage limits because “they rely on powerful server models.” The manufacturer previously outlined that increased access would be available across most iCloud+ subscription plans, and now we have the full details on how this will work.

    Apple says the new system applies to several categories of Apple Intelligence features, including:.

    The usage limits are per device, not per account. This means your iPhone, iPad, and Mac each have separate allowances. Apple isn’t disclosing specific limit numbers. Instead, it says that limits can vary based on the feature, request complexity, system demand, and more.

    As you near your limit, you’ll see an alert within whichever feature you’re using. For example, if you are using Image Playground, a message will appear telling you that you’ve almost hit your usage limit for the day. Once you hit the limit, you’ll be prompted to wait for it to reset or upgrade your iCloud+ strategy.

    Sources indicate that if you hit your limit, basic Siri requests will still work. This includes things like setting timers and alarms. Requests that require Siri to understand personal context and perform more complex, multi-step actions, however, are subject to the limits.

    For example, asking Siri to find the details of an upcoming dinner reservation in your email and add them to your calendar would count toward your daily limit.

    In a recent development, additionally, each device uses its own standard daily usage limit first. After that, it can tap into the additional capacity included with an eligible iCloud+ subscription:.

    Recent findings suggest that the usage unlocked by iCloud+ is shared across all devices signed in to your Apple Account, as well as family members sharing your iCloud+ strategy. The shared usage is available on a first-come, first-served basis.

    In a recent development, all limits will reset daily at the same time, and limits don’t roll over. In most cases, limits reset around midnight in your current time zone.

    Apple has published a support document with more details.

    our 3rd release, a full color 31.5" ePaper display in a handmade wooden frame, is now available for pre-order. watch the short film:.

    According to recent reports, the 1st batch is just ~470 units and i intend to ship at least a few by the end of 2026. most deliveries will happen early 2027. see logistics for more details or pre-order here.

    in 2013 i founded ArtSpot. our vision was to give Upcoming Yorkers a bit of joy by exposing them to local art. we did this through informal agreements with dozens of cafes, small galleries, and restaurants. "let us curate art on your walls, get paid if someone buys it.".

    and it worked. sort of. finding artists was easy, building the platform was easy. getting permission from venues was slow but straightforward. the problem was nobody actually bought the art. i remember the admin email notification that first time a piece was sold. it was a small painting of Janelle Monáe. the buyer was my friend, a gift to me. here it is, still in my possession.

    anyway ArtSpot failed. five years later i paid back my investors (+ 13% interest). but the vision never went away. i love making and consuming art.

    Sources indicate that i probably say "the most popular feature request since launch is ______" too often. after saying no (and yes) to so many requests, it's tough to keep count.

    Industry observers note that but with certainty, one of our strongest convictions was about color. TRMNL is not a television. it is not a clock. we avoid trying to do too much.

    Industry observers note that then grayscale happened. photos look great. art is possible. community member Clark debuted Jaws (yes the movie), 1 frame at a time.

    which got us thinking... maybe we were wrong about color. maybe it aligns with our vision and just maybe, it makes it even bigger.

    Recent findings suggest that today i'm thrilled to bury the lede and announce Frame. it's a 31.5 inch full color ePaper display, enclosed in a hand made wooden body that we manufacture ourselves. yes, we opened our own woodworking shop a few miles from HQ. a closer look at the workshop is coming soon.

    Frame gets all the same features as other TRMNL devices, with a few additional perks spanning both the web platform and the hardware itself. watch the short film or read along below.

    Industry observers note that often requested, always ignored, until now. Frame will enhancement at specified moments of the day versus a relative "every N minutes" cadence. this reduces screen flicker while also extending the battery life and adding continuity to your schedule.

    Sources indicate that the internet is cool but totally unnecessary. Frame's microSD port lets you run devices completely offline with zero personal information reaching our servers.

    In a recent development, like all TRMNL devices, a rechargeable battery is included (10-20k mAh available). but with Frame we added an extra USB-C port on the rear of the device, accessible with a small hole through the back panel for always-on connectivity.

    some of my colleagues are snobs about ePaper dithering algorithms and LUTs (look-up tables). this is now your gain.

    Industry observers note that over the past few months we've been developing Lazarus, a color conversion engine that we think provides Frame the best color matching on the market for any Spectra 6 display. it's also coming soon to our 4-color device, and yes it will be open source for your own tuning pleasure.

    Hang Frame in portrait or landscape orientation without additional hardware, both are built-in and flush mounted. You can optionally buy or build your own kickstand.

    Industry observers note that we're negotiating with some of our favorite community developers to build more Frame-centric features. paying homage to ArtSpot, we just created a Local Art plugin where anyone can submit their work and even sell it through the TRMNL platform.

    Sources indicate that before TRMNL i spent 10 years in b2b software and knew nothing about making physical products for everyday people. nobody ever blasted me on reddit about injection mold flow lines or damaged UPS packages. at best i'd get a G2 review every 3 months.

    It has been revealed that this all changed in July 2024 and after shipping 60,000 devices to 79 countries we've gotten pickier about operational design. chief among these upcoming requirements is doing as much production as possible in-house.

    here are Frame's components and where they're sourced:.

    samples received, design tweaks sent for larger batch.

    TRMNL shop, Pine Mountain, Georgia.

    made-to-order pending wood species chosen at checkout.

    500 in warehouse, includes American + European style adapters.

    made daily from a growing fleet of 3D printers.

    1,000 full assemblies (raw components) in warehouse, bulk pick & place order TBD.

    500 full assemblies ordered, en route next week.

    Samples in warehouse, 800 ordered, en route next week.

    It has been revealed that by reducing complexity, learning from past releases, and having everything we need either in stock or on order, i expect this to be our smoothest fulfillment cycle yet. as with other devices, all Frames are assembled by our own team and never outsourced.

    Batch #1 is available to customers in locations our USA warehouse already ships to: USA, Canada, Mexico, Australia. pre-order here.

    in early 2027 we blueprint to open a 2nd woodworking shop near our Berlin, Germany warehouse to offer postage- and Duty-free fulfillment from a TRMNL team near you.

    #3869. Latest Update: macOS 27.3 includes upcoming privacy controls for Full Disk Access and more

    📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (603 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 9to5mac ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: macOS 27.3 includes upcoming privacy controls for Full Disk Access and more

    📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (603 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Last month, Apple unveiled its intends to tighten macOS privacy controls around Full Disk Access amid the rise of “increasingly capable and autonomous” AI agents.
    • With today’s latest macOS 27.3 beta, Apple is implementing several changes as part of this.
    • In a post on its developer website last month, Apple said some developers are “using Full Disk Access in ways that could put users at risk, exposing everything on their systems.” As such, it said that it would “introduce additional controls to ensure that users who genuinely wish to grant an app this extraordinary level of access can only do so with very explicit user action.”.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Last month, Apple unveiled its intends to tighten macOS privacy controls around Full Disk Access amid the rise of “increasingly capable and autonomous” AI agents.

    With today’s latest macOS 27.3 beta, Apple is implementing several changes as part of this.

    In a post on its developer website last month, Apple said some developers are “using Full Disk Access in ways that could put users at risk, exposing everything on their systems.” As such, it said that it would “introduce additional controls to ensure that users who genuinely wish to grant an app this extraordinary level of access can only do so with very explicit user action.”.

    In macOS 27.2, “Device Control and Data Access” is a unified toggle in System Settings, where Apple indicates that apps with that level of access can “view and send email, edit contacts and photos, monitor your keyboard, track websites, record your screen, control any app on your Mac, and more.”.

    In macOS 27.3, Apple is splitting “Device Control and Data Access” into two categories:.

    According to recent reports, for the latter, consumers will be able to specify which apps an automation tool can access rather than granting it unrestricted control. For instance, you could give an app access to the Mail app, but not Messages.

    macOS 27.3 also adds an option for customers to require an app to request permission every time it needs access, rather than granting it access indefinitely.

    Recent findings suggest that apple is also introducing a new menu bar indicator that will provide additional transparency when an app is controlling another app with System and App Protection Override. This is designed to let users know when an automation tool is interacting with apps and information in the background.

    Recent findings suggest that crucially, Apple isn’t removing the ability to give an app Full Disk Access. If you deem it necessary, you can still give an app Full Disk Access. However, Apple is redesigning the approval process to make the implications of that decision more obvious.

    macOS 27.3 will display a more detailed explanation about the protections being bypassed and the types of personal information that could be exposed.

    In a recent development, owners can also choose to grant an app access to specific folders instead of their entire Mac. For example, an app that only needs to work with files in a particular folder won’t get unrestricted access to everything else.

    Recent findings suggest that any app you’ve already given Full Disk Access will still have that access. Previously granted permissions will remain in effect, and those apps will continue functioning as they do today without any approval required.

    Apple has published a newly introduced support document detailing the Full Disk Access updates.

    Apple indicates the underlying APIs aren’t changing, but developers will need to enhancement their apps to account for situations where users grant limited access rather than unrestricted permissions.

    Finally, Apple notes developers of backup apps and assistive technologies can request entitlements that allow them to maintain the same experience for upcoming installations as before macOS 27.3. Apple has already identified popular apps that rely on these permissions, and those apps will continue working as expected without requiring an entitlement.

    Developers can read more on Apple’s Developer website.

    • In today’s iOS 27.3 beta release, Apple is introducing two changes for iPhone Duo users.
    • Apple is also adding an option to have your iPhone Duo lock when you close it.
    • According to recent reports, you can enable the newly introduced option to unlock your iPhone Duo with the front camera in Settings, under Touch ID & Passcode, after updating to iOS 27.3.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In today’s iOS 27.3 beta release, Apple is introducing two changes for iPhone Duo users. Most notably, it adds a new face recognition option that lets you unlock your iPhone Duo by looking at it.

    Apple is also adding an option to have your iPhone Duo lock when you close it.

    According to recent reports, you can enable the newly introduced option to unlock your iPhone Duo with the front camera in Settings, under Touch ID & Passcode, after updating to iOS 27.3. When enabled, your iPhone Duo will unlock after recognizing your face.

    In the Settings app, Apple says:.

    Industry observers note that use the front camera, along with a recent Touch ID or passcode authentication, to swiftly unlock iPhone Duo when it’s closed. Face recognition data never leaves your device.

    This isn’t Face ID. This new option on iPhone Duo uses the front camera on the outer iPhone Duo display to recognize your face. The iPhone Duo doesn’t have the hardware needed for Face ID.

    Because this isn’t as secure as Face ID, Touch ID, or your passcode, Apple has implemented a few guardrails. First, the setting only works to unlock your iPhone Duo. To use Apple Pay, access your passwords, unlock apps, and do other things that require authentication, you’ll have to use Touch ID or enter your passcode.

    It has been revealed that this face recognition feature also has a time-based limitation. After 45 minutes of inactivity, you have to authenticate with Touch ID or your passcode. That is, if you go 45 minutes without unlocking your iPhone Duo, the facial recognition feature is disabled until you enter your passcode or use Touch ID.

    Industry observers note that finally, this new feature also doesn’t work when using the iPhone Duo unfolded. When unfolded, you still have to use Touch ID or your passcode to unlock the device.

    In a recent development, second, iOS 27.3 adds an option to lock your iPhone Duo when you close it. You can enable this in Settings, under Display & Brightness. Once enabled, your iPhone Duo will lock when you fold, rather than transition from the inner display to the outer display.

    Many iPhone Duo customers (myself included) have remarked Apple should do this. Personally, I’ve been using a shortcut to mimic this behavior, but I’m glad to see that Apple has listened to user feedback and added a default setting for it.

    Latest Update: ‘The only question is if it’s a soft recession or something more dramatic’: Gary Gensler warns the AI bubble is likely to burst and result in a recession before November 2028

    📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1181 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Tomsguide

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • There seems to be a slew of warning signs pointing to the inevitability of the AI bubble bursting a lot sooner than most people think.
    • According to recent reports, the controversial ousting of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang (who happens to be recognized as the "high priest" of the global AI buildout) and the stock market volatility tied to companies that have made huge investments in AI are two of the bigger signs pointing to the AI bubble bursting.
    • One of those individuals is the Former Securities and Exchange Commission Chair, Gary Gensler, who sat down with CNN to give his own take on the possibility of the AI burst event coming to fruition.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    There seems to be a slew of warning signs pointing to the inevitability of the AI bubble bursting a lot sooner than most people think.

    According to recent reports, the controversial ousting of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang (who happens to be recognized as the "high priest" of the global AI buildout) and the stock market volatility tied to companies that have made huge investments in AI are two of the bigger signs pointing to the AI bubble bursting. Plus, there have been plenty of major personalities in the tech and business worlds who have given their thoughts on it becoming a reality at some point.

    One of those individuals is the Former Securities and Exchange Commission Chair, Gary Gensler, who sat down with CNN to give his own take on the possibility of the AI burst event coming to fruition.

    Here’s what he had to say and why his prediction places it near the next presidential election.

    Gensler, who ran the Securities and Exchange Commission from 2021 until 2025, told CNN that today’s AI infrastructure buildout has already crossed into bubble territory and will likely lead into a recession before the next presidential election. "It's already a bubble," the former Wall Street regulator stated. "The only question is if it's a soft recession or something more dramatic.".

    On the topic of all the big spending dedicated to strengthening the current AI infrastructure (which is noted to have reached $800 billion a year by some estimates), Gensler pointed to past trends where major investments in technology eventually stagnate.

    Industry observers note that “History tells us that when you have a upcoming technology and a significant investment ... you come to a point where it plateaus. It retrenches,” Gensler noted. “The only question is if it’s a soft recession or something more dramatic.” The previous instances he cited as big tech investments that eventually met steep declines included railroads, 1920s electricity and the 1990s dot-com boom.

    As for when he sees the AI bubble bursting, he points to it going down sometime before the next presidential election. "I think we're going to have this repricing and a softening of the economy that happens before November 2028," he went on to say. "I can't say exactly when and how stormy, but I would be battening down some hatches.".

    Gensler is among the many other voices in the tech and investment industries who have given their thoughts on the possibilities of the AI bubble bursting and the resulting fallout. Gary Marcus, the former head of AI for Uber, argued to the Financial Times that today’s AI boom is a massive financial bubble driven by unsustainable economics and technological dead ends:.

    It has been revealed that “If there is a deflation of the AI bubble, the optimists say that the newly introduced infrastructure will remain even if the companies do not — just as railways survived the 19th-century railway bust. However, this fails to reckon with the reality of depreciation (few pieces of silicon hold their value for very long because better chips inevitably come along) and the possibility that LLMs could be displaced by more efficient models less dependent on massive numbers of expensive AI chips. In placing massive hyperscaling bets, investors are setting lavish expectations about future earnings. But LLMs are not likely to replicate the near monopolies that have made the market power of current tech giants hard to assail. A better analogy for them might be airlines, which are hobbled by small margins, intense competition, high expenses and dependence on hardware created by outside vendors.” – @garymarcus in @FinancialTimesJune 26, 2026.

    The Canadian mining financier Frank Giustra was quite frank with his AI bubble burst prediction while speaking at this year’s New Orleans Investment Conference. “There will be a reckoning, and some of these companies will get destroyed," he noted. During that same conversation, investor Grant Williams compared the disconnect between recognizing the stock market dangers attached to AI investments and taking proper precautions to a natural disaster.

    It has been revealed that "If we told you a hurricane was heading to Fresh Orleans, everybody would take precautions," he explained. "The interesting thing about stock market bubbles is people don't really think about what can go wrong. They're still thinking about making money.".

    According to recent reports, while many voices are speaking on the very real possibility of an AI bubble burst, there are business bigwigs who have made it clear that everyone shouldn’t be all that worried about it. During a sit-down interview with CNBC, Amazon founder Jeff Bezos tried to ease everyone’s fears about such a financially devastating event coming to pass. “Even if it does turn out to be a bubble, you shouldn’t worry about it because the bubble is driving investment and a lot of the investment is going to turn out to be very healthy,” he proclaimed.

    Bret Taylor, the chairman of OpenAI and CEO of Sierra, spoke to The Verge and flat-out acknowledged that an AI bubble exists while still noting that it's totally fine. And while speaking to CNBC at the 2026 World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland, his AI optimism pointed to a scenario where the market will correct itself as weaker industry players and overfunded ventures will fall by the wayside.

    Sources indicate that “When everyone knows that AI is going to have a huge impact on the economy across a huge range of industries and workflows, money is plentiful,” Taylor noted. “I think over the next few years, you’ll see a correction, you also see consolidation, but I don’t think you can get innovation without that kind of messy competition.”.

    Gensler’s prophetic words about the AI bubble bursting before we even reach the next presidential election are alarming, yes.

    But I can envision a world where potential candidates use that moment as one of their political talking points in a bid to ease back on all that AI spending, put more into the American populace and hold back on bailing out any of the AI companies that are hurting from such a traumatic event.

    All signs point to something devastating happening to the AI industry at some point, especially with the huge backlash against data centers and the politicians who are looking to put in moratoriums on their continued development.
